title: How well do dementia risk scores predict dementia? A systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: In our systematic review and meta-analysis, we aimed to assess the predictive accuracy and clinical applicability of ten dementia risk assessment scores for incident dementia in cohort studies. Three of 10 risk scores had sufficient, comparable data for a meta-analysis. We analyzed the Cardiovascular Risk Factors Ageing and Dementia (CAIDE), Lifestyle for brain health (LIBRA), and Alzheimer's Disease Risk Index (ANU-ADRI) in middle- and older-aged baseline populations with short, medium, and long follow-up durations, starting free from dementia, with or without other health conditions. A total of 29 studies met our inclusion criteria; 13 were included in the meta-analyses. CAIDE performed best, particularly among middle-aged participants at baseline, with longer follow-up periods, yielding pooled areas under the curves (AUCs) of 0.74-0.76. ANU-ADRI showed stable, moderate predictive accuracy with AUCs of approximately 0.65-0.71. The original LIBRA showed the lowest discrimination, with AUCs ranging from 0.51 to 0.60, whereas the modified LIBRA performed better, with AUCs of 0.65-0.67 at short follow-up and a pooled AUC of 0.70 (95% CI 0.66-0.74) at medium follow-up. Dementia risk assessment scales show variable predictive performance across scores, baseline age, and follow-up duration, and may be useful for dementia risk stratification in clinical practice. As a substantial proportion of dementia risk is linked to potentially modifiable factors, identifying high-risk individuals may help guide timely risk-reduction strategies. Further prospective validation is needed across different populations and clinical settings.

title: On the precision of timing during joint rushing.
abstract: When individuals synchronize their movements during joint actions, they systematically accelerate the prescribed tempo: the so-called joint rushing phenomenon. While research has focused on the resulting drift in accuracy, it remains unexplored whether interpersonal synchronization also affects precision of timing. Pooling together 110 participants from three independent finger-tapping experiments, this study addresses this gap by analyzing the Weber fraction, the standard deviation of the tapping errors relative to interval duration, by comparing Solo and Joint synchronization in sub-second durations. The results revealed that joint synchronization causes a dramatic, duration-scaled degradation of accuracy (rushing), yet imposes only a small, roughly duration-independent cost on precision, whose non-linear profile across durations was overall preserved in both conditions. This pattern suggests that interpersonal synchronization largely affects period correction while overall preserving phase correction, a distinction relevant to current theoretical models of temporal coordination in social behavior. OPEN PRACTICES STATEMENT: The raw data and the analysis codes are available via the Open Science Framework at: https://osf.io/jxs3d/overview . The experiments were not preregistered.

title: Understanding Neurogenic Patient-Ventilator Discordance and its Management.
abstract: Patients with an acutely injured brain may resist the mechanical physics of the ventilator. Neurogenic respiratory breathing patterns generated by the patient may result in the ventilator failing to synchronize with this abnormal drive. This asynchrony may be perceived as distress and with a high respiratory drive could also lead to global lung stress and diaphragmatic myoinjury, and affect liberation from the mechanical ventilator at a later point. Patient-ventilator synchrony concerns have rarely been prioritized in neurocritical care guidelines and are often inappropriately treated with escalating sedation. Starting with the essentials of waveform interpretation and moving towards more complex interpretations of these asynchronies, this review provides insight into the common themes of neurogenic synchrony concerns in mechanically ventilated patients. High respiratory drive, double-triggering/ breath-stacking, and reverse triggering are the most prevalent observations. Adjusting the ventilator can improve patient-ventilator interaction and a number of options to remediate these synchrony concerns are provided.

title: Impaired cortical inhibition in blepharospasm: evidence from reduced short-latency afferent inhibition and shortened cortical silent period.
journal: Neurological sciences : official journal of the Italian Neurological Society and of the Italian Society of Clinical Neurophysiology
abstract: Blepharospasm (BSP) is a neural network disorder with poorly understood cortical electrophysiological mechanisms. To investigate intracortical excitability and sensorimotor pathways in BSP patients and evaluate the effects of botulinum toxin A (BoNT-A) on cortical activity. Thirty BSP patients and 20 healthy controls underwent single- and paired-pulse transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) to assess indices including SAI, CSP, SICI, and ICF. Sixteen treatment-naive patients were reassessed one month post-BoNT-A injection. BSP patients showed significantly reduced SAI and shortened CSP compared to controls. Impaired SAI strongly correlated with disease severity scores (BFMDRS and GDSRS: r ranging from 0.514 to0.782, p < 0.01). SICI and ICF showed no group differences. Furthermore, BoNT-A treatment failed to reverse these central cortical abnormalities.Notably, these deficits were recorded from the clinically unaffected abductor pollicis brevis muscle and therefore represent widespread cortical trait markers rather direct evidence of dysfunction within the eyelid circuit itself. BSP is characterized by impaired cortical inhibition that is consistent with cholinergic dysfunction. BoNT-A relieves symptoms peripherally without altering fundamental central cortical excitability.The cortical deficits, recorded from an unaffected limb, indicate a generalised rather than eyelid-specific abnormality.

title: Shared control-network recruitment and task-dependent brain-behavior associations in bilingual language and rule switching.
abstract: Bilingual language control is thought to draw on domain-general cognitive control, yet it remains unclear whether cross-task overlap in neural recruitment is accompanied by similar brain-behavior relationships. Previous connectivity studies have typically estimated functional connectivity (FC) across entire tasks or blocks, obscuring network changes specific to switch trials. We combined hierarchical drift-diffusion modeling, regional activation, and beta-series FC in 126 Chinese-English bilinguals (123 with usable fMRI data) who completed language- and rule-switching tasks. Both tasks reduced drift rates and prolonged nondecision times on switch trials. They also recruited a common 28-region switch-sensitive control core and showed increased switch-related FC within this core and between the core and default mode, subcortical, and cerebellar systems. At the individual-difference level, generalized estimating equations revealed task-dependent brain-behavior relationships: core-within and core-subcortical FC were more positively associated with drift-rate switch cost during language switching than during rule switching. Together, the results identify partial overlap in regional recruitment, similarly directed system-level FC changes, and distinct FC-evidence-accumulation relationships across tasks.

title: Turing-like tests for language and vision demonstrate a narrowing gap between humans and AI.
abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) becomes increasingly embedded in daily life, ascertaining whether an agent is human is critical. Here we systematically benchmark AI's ability to imitate humans in three language tasks (image captioning, word association and conversation) and three vision tasks (colour estimation, object detection and attention prediction), collecting data from n = 636 humans and 37 AI agents. We also conducted 72,191 Turing-like tests with 1,916 human judges and 10 AI judges. Current AIs are approaching the ability to convincingly impersonate humans and deceive human judges in both language and vision. Even simple AI judges outperformed humans in distinguishing AI from human responses. Imitation ability showed minimal correlation with conventional AI performance metrics, suggesting that passing as human is an important independent evaluation criterion. The large-scale Turing-like datasets and metrics introduced here offer valuable benchmarks for assessing human-likeness in AI and highlight the importance of rigorous, quantitative imitation tests for AI development.

title: Serum neurofilament light protein as a biomarker across the cognitive decline continuum: a cross-sectional study from an Indian cohort.
abstract: The Alzheimer's disease (AD) continuum spans from healthy aging to subjective cognitive decline (SCD), mild cognitive impairment (MCI), and dementia. Serum Neurofilament Light Protein (NfL) is a potential non-invasive biomarker for neurodegeneration. This study evaluates serum NfL across the cognitive decline continuum in an Indian cohort. To assess serum NfL as a biomarker for early and progressive neurodegeneration, including its diagnostic utility in SCD, MCI, and AD. This case-control study included 129 participants: 28 cognitively normal older adults (HC), 32 with SCD, 33 with MCI, and 36 with AD. Serum NfL levels were measured using Simoa® technology. The association of NfL with cognitive decline was analyzed using a Generalized Linear Model (GLM) adjusted for age and sex, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves assessed diagnostic performance. Serum NfL median levels progressively increased across groups: HC (21.1 pg/mL), SCD (28.94 pg/mL), MCI (35.5 pg/mL), and AD (48.64 pg/mL). Compared to HC, NfL levels were significantly higher in SCD (adjusted coefficient: 0.59, p = 0.004), MCI (0.72, p = 0.001), and AD (1.13, p < 0.001). ROC analysis showed good discrimination: AUC was 0.795 for SCD vs. HC, 0.908 for MCI vs.HC, and 0.941 for AD vs. HC. The study demonstrates a clear association between rising serum NfL levels and advancing cognitive decline. Serum NfL demonstrated potential as a sensitive and non-invasive biomarker for early detection and staging of cognitive decline. The establishment of population-specific cut-offs within an Indian cohort contributes to global efforts toward standardizing blood-based biomarkers for AD.

title: Effect of Oral Creatine Supplementation on Plasma, Central, and Peripheral Creatine Levels in Creatine Transporter Deficiency Mice.
abstract: Creatine transporter deficiency (CRTD) is characterized by severe brain creatine depletion due to creatine transporter (CRT) dysfunction. Although oral creatine supplementation has been explored as a therapy, its effects under CRT-deficient conditions remain unclear. Here, we aimed to investigate the impact of oral creatine supplementation on creatine distribution in plasma, brain, and peripheral tissues using CRTD model mice. Creatine was orally administered for 30 days to creatine transporter knockout (Slc6a8-/y, CRT-KO) male mice, knock-in male mice harboring a patient-derived G561R mutation (Slc6a8G561R/y, CRT-KI), and wild-type male mice (WT). Oral creatine supplementation significantly increased plasma creatine in both CRT-KO and CRT-KI mice but failed to restore creatine levels in the brain. Conversely, creatine levels increased markedly in the liver and kidney. Urinary creatine and the creatine-to-creatinine ratio, a key diagnostic biomarker for CRTD, were substantially elevated, exceeding diagnostic thresholds even in WT mice. Oral creatine increases systemic creatine but fails to restore brain creatine under CRT-deficient conditions, underscoring the crucial role of CRT-mediated blood-brain barrier (BBB) uptake and the need to restore creatine transport across the BBB to elevate brain creatine levels. Furthermore, creatine intake should be controlled for proper diagnostic biomarker interpretation.

title: Adult attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder symptoms are associated with chronic low back pain: a nationwide cross-sectional study of 2113 individuals.
journal: European spine journal : official publication of the European Spine Society, the European Spinal Deformity Society, and the European Section of the Cervical Spine Research Society
abstract: Low back pain (LBP) is a major contributor to reduced quality of life and increasing global healthcare burdens. Recently, adult attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) has been associated with chronic pain interference. In this study, we examined the prevalence and characteristics of ADHD symptoms in the general population and their association with LBP. This nationwide cross-sectional observational study included 2,113 participants from a survey of randomly selected residents aged ≥ 20 years. Self-reported ADHD symptoms were assessed using the Adult ADHD Self-Report Scale (ASRS), a screening instrument for possible ADHD in adults. Perceived stress and psychological distress were assessed with the Perceived Stress Scale (PSS) and the Kessler 6-Item Psychological Distress Scale (K6), respectively. Participants were grouped by LBP status as no LBP, acute/subacute LBP, or chronic LBP, and multinomial logistic regression was used to identify the factors associated with each; models with and without the PSS and K6 were compared. A positive ADHD screen was identified in 3.27% of participants, of whom 23.2% reported chronic LBP compared with 11.0% of screen-negative participants. A higher ASRS score was associated with chronic LBP after adjustment (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 1.255 per 10-point increase, 95% confidence interval 1.051-1.509, p = 0.010), as were older age, comorbidity burden, smoking, and the PSS and K6 scores. None of the psychosocial measures was associated with acute/subacute LBP. The aOR for the ASRS score fell from 1.548 to 1.255 when the PSS and K6 were added to the model but remained significant. A positive ADHD screen on the ASRS was identified in 3.27% of participants from the general population, and a higher score for self-reported adult ADHD symptoms remained statistically associated with chronic LBP after adjustment for established associated factors, including perceived stress and psychological distress.

title: Microglial NUS1 deficiency drives dopaminergic neurodegeneration through intercellular iron dysregulation in Parkinson's disease models.
abstract: The selective loss of dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra pars compacta is a defining feature of Parkinson's disease (PD), yet its underlying mechanisms remain unclear. NUS1, which encodes neurite outgrowth inhibitor-B receptor (NgBR), was recently identified as a PD risk gene. Here we show that NgBR is highly expressed in microglia, where its deficiency drives progressive PD-like motor deficits and dopaminergic neurodegeneration via the LCN2-SLC22A17 iron-transport axis in mice. NgBR deficiency in mouse and human microglia triggers endoplasmic reticulum stress and PERK-ATF4-NUPR1 signaling, which preferentially induces LCN2-mediated iron efflux over cytokine release. Subsequently, microglia-derived iron-loaded Holo-LCN2, but not iron-free Apo-LCN2, is internalized by SLC22A17, a receptor highly expressed in dopaminergic neurons, leading to iron overload and ferroptosis. Pharmacological inhibition of LCN2-SLC22A17 axis or ferroptosis alleviated dopaminergic neuron loss and PD-like symptoms caused by microglial NgBR deficiency in vitro and in vivo. Our findings identify disrupted intercellular iron homeostasis as a pathological driver of PD and highlight the LCN2-SLC22A17 axis as a potential therapeutic target.

title: Chronic progressive demyelination induces a microglial state with lysosomal dysfunction.
abstract: Dysfunctional immune responses impair remyelination and contribute to neurodegeneration. While immune and metabolic responses to acute myelin injury are well characterized, myeloid cell adaptations to chronic myelin damage remain poorly understood. Here we performed a comparative analysis of genetic and toxic mouse models of acute and chronic demyelination, which identified a distinct microglial state associated with chronic demyelination, characterized by sustained pro-inflammatory activation, lysosomal lipid sequestration and reduced lipid droplet formation. Transcriptomics profiling further revealed a metabolic program marked by upregulated cholesterol synthesis and diminished sterol efflux. Treatment with a desmosterol mimetic possessing 24-dehydrocholesterol reductase inhibitor activity reversed this microglial state, attenuated pro-inflammatory signaling (including C-C Motif Chemokine Ligand 4 expression), reduced myelin damage and improved motor performance in a mouse model of leukodystrophy. Our findings uncover a pro-inflammatory microglial state characterized by lysosomal dysfunction and increased myelin reactivity, highlighting a novel therapeutic target for chronic demyelinating disorders.

title: Use of animal models to understand CNS neuroimmunology - guidance from the International Society for Neuroimmunology White Paper Task Force.
abstract: Neuroimmunology is a rapidly expanding field in which many breakthroughs have been fuelled by studies in animal models that capture aspects of human neurological disease. However, the variety of animal models available, with their relative merits and drawbacks, is not well documented in the literature, posing a hurdle for scientists who are venturing into the world of neuroimmunology. Moreover, nuances between animal models, their utility for studying neuroimmunological processes and the variables that affect their associated clinical and pathological outcomes can affect the reproducibility and clinical relevance of findings at the preclinical stage. In this Review, the International Society of Neuroimmunology White Paper Task Force describes animal models that can be used to study neuroimmunological aspects of neurological disease and the intrinsic and extrinsic factors that affect readouts from these models. We provide guidance on how to manipulate these factors to gain insight into neuroimmunology and to control them for improved reproducibility. We also consider the advantages and limitations of available tools, including robust genetic systems, neuroimmunological imaging, functional readouts and omics-based cell profiling. Finally, we discuss how animal models have advanced drug development to treat neuroimmunological diseases and how the same principles can provide insight into a variety of neurological disorders. We aim to provide guidance on how to optimize the use of animal models to gain insight into neuroimmunological mechanisms and support the preclinical drug discovery pipeline.

title: Digital Health Interventions for Falls Prevention in Older People.
abstract: Implementation of falls prevention programs at scale remains challenging due to resource constraints, clinic dependency and inequitable access. We critically review digital health technologies and map these to the World Falls Guidelines (WFG) risk-stratified pathway, from risk screening to intervention delivery, appraising the evidence, clinical readiness and implementation challenges. Self-managed digital exercise programs have the strongest evidence base, with three trials demonstrating reductions in falls among community-living older people and economic data supporting cost-effectiveness in those with a history of falls. Other technologies demonstrate feasibility, but none has demonstrated falls reduction in adequately powered trials. Implementation evidence is emerging but concentrated in high-income, digitally literate populations. Mapped to the WFG pathway, digital exercise programs are ready for routine implementation; realising broader potential requires regulatory frameworks that set evidence standards for digital products, funding models that support digital care and sustained commitment to equitable access across the diversity of older people.

title: Nerve activity initiates autoimmune hair loss.
Giving AI a seat at the peer review table.
Body image distress in women and men with advanced pancreatic cancer approaching death - post-hoc analyses from the MISTRAL-trial.
journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
abstract: Weight loss is common in individuals with pancreatic cancer. The aim of the present study was to address how body image distress and weight worries change over time as death approaches in patients with pancreatic cancer, and whether there are gender differences. Post-hoc analyses were performed using data from the MISTRAL-trial. Body image distress and weight worries were assessed using the European Organisation for Research and Treatment of Cancer (EORTC) QLQ-PAN-26-questionnaire as part of the original trial. Data were used to assess body image distress and weight worries at time points corresponding to 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, and 6 months prior to death. Mixed-effects linear models with random intercepts were used to examine trajectories of body image distress and weight worries in women and men. We analysed data from 125 participants, of whom 64 (51.2%) were women. Both body image distress and weight worries increased over time during the 6 months preceding death, β = 3.54, 95%CI: 1.67- 5.41; and β = 2.98, 95%CI: 0.53- 5.44, respectively. There were no statistically significant sex differences in the rate of change although women tended to report higher body image distress closer to death and men higher weight worries across all time points. Increased body image distress and weight loss concerns observed in both women and men with pancreatic cancer at the end of life highlight the importance of addressing these issues in palliative care.

title: Neural limits of temporal feature binding in human visual cortex.
abstract: Humans are able to track the change of color and orientation (CO) of an object at a stunning rate. However, spatially separating those features slows this rate by an order of magnitude - a temporal limit of feature binding that is little understood. Here, we investigate the underlying mechanisms using high-temporal resolution cortical source localization of the magnetic field response elicited by CO-pairs alternating at different frequencies in color and orientation. We show that (1) binding requires a rapid recurrent modulation (~120 ms) of activity in V1/V2, whose latency is independent of the alternation rate. (2) Performance drops to chance when the alternation rate becomes too high to accommodate the recurrent process within a single alternation. (3) CO binding itself is mediated by color-based attention, which gradually biases re-occurring CO combinations containing the attended color. These observations together demonstrate that CO-binding across space depends on rapid recurrent processing in early visual cortex, with its temporal limit being set by the time this process takes to be completed. Binding ultimately results from a slower and gradual attentional bias of the recurrent process instantiating a form of stroboscopic stationarity in the stream of alternations for unambiguous discrimination of the correct feature-combination.

title: The intermediate hippocampus integrates shock-observation and spatial information during observational fear memory in male rats.
abstract: Learning where danger lurks by observing others requires linking another individual's distress to one's own representation of space. How the hippocampus implements this mapping is unknown. We recorded Neuropixels activity across the dorsal, intermediate and ventral hippocampus of male rats during contextual fear learning by observation, subsequent rest and recall. Observers showed increased immobility in the context where they had witnessed a conspecific receive footshocks, with substantial inter-individual variability. Pyramidal neurons were recruited by shock observation, with enriched shock-excited cells in the intermediate hippocampus. In the dorsal and intermediate hippocampus, shock-observation responses scaled with baseline place-field firing, revealing a gain-like conjunctive code between observed distress and observer's position. Following learning, shock-context spatial representations were selectively stabilized in the intermediate hippocampus, and post-learning sharp-wave ripples preferentially reactivated shock-context ensembles, especially in animals expressing contextual freezing. These findings identify candidate hippocampal mechanisms by which socially acquired threat information are mapped onto the observer's spatial representation and consolidated into memory.

title: Neuromuscular junction pathology in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis and emerging molecular therapeutic strategies.
abstract: Traditionally conceptualized as a soma-centric pathology, amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a fatal, heterogeneous neurodegenerative disease. The suboptimal outcomes of central nervous system (CNS)-directed therapeutic strategies have necessitated a shift in focus toward the dying-back hypothesis. This hypothesis contends that synaptic disconnection and axonal retraction at the distal neuromuscular junction (NMJ) are early pathological events that may antedate overt motor neuron loss. This review systematically examines the NMJ as an early vulnerable and therapeutically tractable peripheral niche in ALS pathogenesis, rather than merely a downstream consequence of proximal proteinopathy. Evidence from human clinical samples and ALS mouse models, particularly SOD1-G93A mice, collectively supports the early vulnerability of the NMJ, with the temporal precedence of denervation, synaptic retraction, and mitochondrial dysfunction most clearly demonstrated in experimental models. We highlight how the breakdown of the tripartite synapse-comprising the motor terminal, skeletal muscle, and terminal Schwann cells (tSCs)-may disrupt essential neurotrophic signaling and local metabolic homeostasis. Furthermore, we discuss how advancements in humanized in vitro NMJ models and spatial transcriptomics provide unprecedented resolution into localized RNA dysmetabolism and bioenergetic failure. Finally, we evaluate emerging therapeutic strategies specifically designed to stabilize or restore the NMJ, including MuSK agonists and other NMJ-directed approaches. By recontextualizing the NMJ as a critical early site of vulnerability, we propose that targeting the peripheral synaptic microenvironment may offer a promising strategy for modifying the progression of ALS.

title: Deep brain stimulation ameliorates social deficits from early-life pain by restoring excitatory/inhibitory balance in the anterior cingulate cortex.
abstract: The neural mechanisms underlying how early-life pain leads to long-term impairments in adult social deficit remain largely elusive. Here, by establishing a juvenile inflammatory pain model in mice and employing a combination of neuromodulation techniques, we found that early-life pain experience induces a specific and enduring social deficit in adulthood. This deficit originates from a persistent excitatory/inhibitory (E/I) imbalance within the anterior cingulate cortex (ACC). Specifically, during social interaction, we observed diminished activity in ACC excitatory neurons alongside hyperfunction of inhibitory GABAergic neurons, resulting in insufficient synaptic glutamate release. Targeted metabolomics analysis further confirmed aberrant levels of glutamate and GABA within the ACC. Targeting this mechanism, we demonstrated that either enhancing ACC excitation or dampening its inhibition via optogenetic and chemogenetic manipulations effectively rescued the social deficit. Importantly, deep brain stimulation (DBS) targeting the ACC also activated excitatory neurons and successfully reversed this social deficit. This study unveils a core mechanism whereby early-life pain impairs social function by inducing a state of hypoexcitation and hyperinhibition in the ACC. Furthermore, we establish that DBS can effectively rectify this ACC imbalance, providing a novel theoretical basis and a potential translational strategy for intervening in social deficits associated with developmental trauma.

title: Independent basal ganglia neural populations encode speech production and ambient-noise levels.
abstract: The basal ganglia's (BG) contribution to motor control is thought to involve invigorating movement based on environmental constraints, yet this has primarily been studied in the limb system. We hypothesized that the BG similarly regulate the respiratory and articulatory systems during speech. We recorded local field potentials and single-unit activity from the subthalamic nucleus (STN) and globus pallidus (GP) in humans during a speech task where the Lombard Effect was used to modulate environmental constraints. GP and STN exhibited distinct temporal profiles during speech production. Neither region robustly encoded produced speech intensity. Instead, neural populations tracked ambient background noise levels, even during baseline, with high decoding accuracy. The ambient-noise-modulated sites were an independent population from speech-modulated sites. We theorize that the code is leveraged in downstream BG-cortical loop nodes to invigorate speech oro-motor gestures and co-speech manual limb gestures, both of which respond to ambient noise levels to maintain high-fidelity communication.

title: Microglia regulate nucleus accumbens synaptic development and circuit function underlying threat avoidance behaviors in mice.
abstract: While microglia are well known for pruning synapses during neurodevelopment, their role in synapse formation remains understudied. Here we investigate how microglial absence impacts synaptic development in the nucleus accumbens (NAc), a region critical for emotional regulation and motivated behaviors. Using genetically modified mice lacking microglia (Csf1rΔFIRE/ΔFIRE), we find blunted excitatory synapse formation in the NAc, particularly during the second and third postnatal weeks. Tissue-level NAc proteomics in the third postnatal week reveals changes in proteins involved in synapse structure, trans-synaptic signaling, and pre-synaptic function. Although electrophysiological changes largely resolve by adulthood, microglia-lacking mice exhibit persistent changes in threat avoidance behavior and underlying NAc neuronal activity. Transient depletion of NAc microglia during the second postnatal week similarly disrupts synapse formation and adult threat avoidance. Together, these findings identify a role for microglia in shaping NAc synaptic development and in establishing functional circuits that support adult behavioral function.

title: Cortex-wide laminar dynamics diverge during learning.
abstract: Learning to link sensory information to motor actions requires coordinated activity across the cerebral cortex, but how different cortical layers contribute to learning remains unclear. Here we show that learning engages distinct, layer-specific activity patterns across the cortex of male mice during acquisition of a whisker-based go/no-go task. Using wide-field calcium imaging of either layer 2/3 or layer 5 neurons across 25 cortical areas, we found that learning produced markedly different, and sometimes opposing, changes in activity between layers. Layer 5 exhibited widespread suppression before sensory input and enhanced activity in frontal cortex during sensorimotor transformation, whereas layer 2/3 showed learning-related enhancements in higher-order sensory areas during sensation. In contrast, both layers displayed similar learning-related enhancement in barrel cortex during whisker touch. These findings reveal complementary roles of superficial and deep cortical layers during learning and demonstrate that layer-specific cortical dynamics are a fundamental feature of sensorimotor learning.

title: Cortical dynamics in Angelman syndrome: novel insights from a preclinical mouse model.
abstract: Angelman syndrome (AS) is a neurogenetic disorder caused by the loss of function in the maternally inherited UBE3A gene, leading to a spectrum of symptoms that include developmental delays, intellectual disability, and motor impairments. While genetic and molecular mechanisms of AS are increasingly well characterized, a critical gap remains in understanding how disruptions in neuronal connectivity at the circuit level contribute to its pathophysiology. Here, we aimed to address this gap by investigating cortical connectivity alterations in a mouse model of AS. Using wide-field calcium imaging, we monitored real-time neuronal activity across the entire dorsal cortex in awake animals. Our results revealed widespread cortical hyperconnectivity in AS mice compared to wild-type controls, particularly in regions involved in motor and sensory processing. Notably, this pattern of aberrant connectivity persisted across two distinct time points in adulthood, suggesting a stable and enduring network dysfunction. These findings indicate that the absence of UBE3A function drives persistent disruptions of functional connectivity, which may underlie key clinical manifestations of AS.

title: Combatting nonidentifiability to infer motor cortex inputs yields similar encoding of initial and corrective movements.
abstract: Primary motor cortex (M1) plays a central role in voluntary movement, but how it integrates sensory-driven corrective instructions is unclear. We analyzed population activity recorded from M1 of male macaques during a sequential arm movement task with target updates requiring online adjustments to the motor plan. Using Latent Factor Analysis via Dynamical Systems (LFADS), we separated neural activity into two components: intrinsic dynamics and inferred external inputs. Inferred input timing was more strongly locked to target appearance than to movement onset, suggesting that variable reaction times reflect interactions between inputs and ongoing dynamics. Inferred inputs were tuned similarly for initial and corrective movements, suggesting shared input encoding across visually-instructed and corrective movements previously obscured by M1 dynamics. Because input inference can suffer from nonidentifiability, where different models fit data indistinguishably, we used ensembles of models with varied hyperparameters to diagnose when inputs are identifiable or nonidentifiable. In the monkey data, ensembles produced consistently similar results, suggesting that inputs could be meaningfully inferred and that their encoding was not simply a result of model bias. These results highlight the challenges of nonidentifiability and the potential of model ensembles to identify inputs in ongoing dynamics, at least in some cases.

title: Microglial deletion induces despair-like behavior associated with astrogliosis.
abstract: Microglia, the brain's resident immune cells, are increasingly recognized as key regulators of brain physiology and behavior. However, their specific role in affective states remains controversial, with studies reporting conflicting depression-like outcomes following their removal. Using the colony stimulating factor-1 receptor (CSF1R) inhibitor PLX5622 in adult mice of both sexes, we found that microglial deletion selectively induced despair-like behavior (increased immobility in the forced swim test and the tail suspension test) in either sex, without affecting locomotion, anxiety, sociability, anhedonia, or cognition. This effect was accompanied by reactive astrogliosis in the medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC). Unexpectedly, microglial deletion induced a predominant A2-like astrocyte reactivity. Notably, both the despair-like and A2-like phenotypes resolved upon microglia repopulation. Critically, pharmacological inhibition of these hyperactive mPFC astrocytes with fluorocitrate reversed the despair-like phenotype, indicating that microglial loss triggers maladaptive astrocyte reactivity that drives behavioral despair. Our results reveal an essential role for microglia in maintaining emotional homeostasis, possibly through interaction with astrocytes.

title: Brasenia schreberi Polysaccharides: Extraction, Structural Characterization, and Immunomodulatory Activity.
abstract: Brasenia schreberi, a valuable aquatic vegetable in East Asia prized for its unique and delicious taste, is rich in bioactive compounds, including polysaccharides, proteins, vitamins, and trace elements. This study compared enzymatic and alkaline extraction techniques to isolate polysaccharides from B. schreberi. Extraction yield, total sugar, protein, uronic acid contents, and monosaccharide composition were determined, and structural characteristics were analyzed using Fourier-transform infrared (FT-IR) spectroscopy. Following alkaline extraction, the crude polysaccharide (BSP-A) was then purified by DEAE-52 cellulose and Sepharose CL-6B chromatography to obtain a homogeneous fraction, BSP-2, with a molecular weight of 544.2 kDa. The physicochemical properties and structure of BSP-2 were analyzed using comprehensive techniques including FT-IR, Congo red assay, scanning electron microscope (SEM), high performance liquid chromatography (HPLC), gas chromatography mass spectrometry (GC-MS), methylation analysis, and thermogravimetric analysis. Results showed that BSP-2 is a flat, sheet-like polysaccharide devoid of a triple-helix structure. It comprises nine monosaccharides, including mannose, rhamnose, glucuronic acid, galacturonic acid, glucose, galactose, xylose, arabinose, and fucose, via 18 distinct glycosidic bond types of linkage. Rheological tests of BSP-2 indicated the gel-like behavior at low angular frequencies and the fluid-like behavior at high frequencies. Additionally, the immunomodulatory activities of BSP-2 on the RAW264.7 macrophage cells were investigated, with key assessments of cytotoxicity, nitric oxide (NO) production, the mRNA expression levels of various cytokines, and the expression of key proteins in the mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) pathway. These results establish a foundational framework for the extraction and identification of polysaccharides from B. schreberi and demonstrate their value in immunoregulatory applications.

title: [Theoretical system of brain-computer interface for basic research].
journal: Sheng wu yi xue gong cheng xue za zhi = Journal of biomedical engineering = Shengwu yixue gongchengxue zazhi
abstract: Brain-computer interface (BCI) has achieved remarkable progress in brain signal acquisition, decoding algorithms, and related fields. Nevertheless, its underlying theoretical system remains largely fragmented, lacking a systematic characterization of system decodability, performance boundaries, and dynamic constraint mechanisms. To address this gap, this paper formalizes BCI systems as a closed-loop probabilistic information processing model from the perspectives of information theory and statistical decision-making. This paper constructs a foundational theoretical system consisting of scientific hypotheses, neuroscience principles, fundamental theorems, and basic laws, derives four results capable of guiding experimental design, and illustrates the application boundaries with reference to motor imagery BCI paradigms. This theoretical system is expected to provide a unified analytical benchmark for basic BCI research and drive the paradigm shift of BCI from engineering experience-driven algorithm optimization to theory-driven system analysis and design.

title: [Withaferin A inhibits biofilm formation and adhesion of neonatal meningitis Escherichia coli by downregulating ibeR expression].
journal: Nan fang yi ke da xue xue bao = Journal of Southern Medical University
abstract: To investigate the effect of Withaferin A (WA) on biofilm formation and adhesion of neonatal meningitis Escherichia coli (NMEC) and the regulatory role of ibeR. CCK-8 assay was used to determine the sub-inhibitory concentration of WA in cultured human brain microvascular endothelial cells (HBMECs). The NMEC strain RS218 (E44) and an ibeR deletion mutant (BR2) were treated with 1, 2, and 5 μmol/L WA, and the changes in biofilm formation were evaluated by crystal violet staining and SBF assay; the expression levels of ibeR, ibeA, and ibeT were detected by qPCR. HBMECs co-cultured with E44 or BR2 were examined for bacterial adhesion, and indole production in the supernatants and the effect of exogenous indole on biofilm formation were evaluated. Based on cytotoxicity test, 2 μmol/L WA was used for subsequent experiments. WA dose-dependently reduced biofilm formation in E44 but not in the BR2 strain but did not significantly inhibit proliferation of either strain. WA treatment significantly downregulated ibeR expression in the bacteria. Deletion of ibeR did not affect bacterial growth but significantly decreased biofilm formation and adhesion to HBMECs. WA treatment also reduced cell adhesion ability of E44, which was not observed in BR2. WA significantly increased indole production and decreased biofilm content in E44 but not in BR2. IbeR regulates NMEC biofilm formation and adhesion likely by modulating indole production. WA dose-dependently inhibits biofilm and adhesion of NMEC by downregulating ibeR without affecting bacterial growth.

title: [Jiaotaiwan improves lipid metabolism abnormalities in a mouse model of Alzheimer disease by regulating the AMPK signaling pathway].
journal: Nan fang yi ke da xue xue bao = Journal of Southern Medical University
abstract: To explore whether Jiaotaiwan ameliorates Alzheimer disease (AD) by regulating lipid metabolism via the AMPK pathway. Twenty 3-month-old male transgenic APP/PS1 mice were randomized equally into two groups for treatment with Jiaotaiwan or normal saline via gavage for 4 weeks, with 10 saline-treated wild-type C57BL/6J mice as the control group. Brain lipid deposition, plasma and brain TC, TG and NEFA levels, and expressions of BACE1, Aβ, p-Tau, ZO-1, occludin, AMPK/p-AMPK, SREBP1, ACC, ATGL, and APOE in the brain tissues were detected. In the in vitro experiment, PC12 cell co-cultured with mature adipocytes were treated with Jiaotaiwan, AICAR, or both, and the intracellular lipid droplets, TG, NEFA, AMPK activity, and ACC expression were measured. In the AD mouse models, Jiaotaiwan significantly reduced brain lipid deposits, lowered plasma TC and TG levels, increased plasma NEFA level, and decreased brain TG and NEFA expressions without affecting TC expression. Jiaotaiwan treatment also significantly lowered the expressions of cerebral Aβ and p-Tau, increased cerebral occludin expression and p-AMPK/AMPK ratio, and reduced ACC, SREBP1 and APOE expressions without affecting ATGL expression in the mouse models. In the co-cultured cells, Jiaotaiwan obviously alleviated cellular lipid accumulation, lowered cellular TG and NEFA levels, reduced supernatant TG content, and enhanced NEFA release. In both the AD mouse model and co-cultured cell model, Jiaotaiwan significantly lowered Aβ level, increased AMPK activity and p-AMPK/AMPK expression, and lowered the expressions of ACC. Jiaotaiwan combined with AICAR produced a synergistic effect for enhancing p-AMPK/AMPK expressions in the co-cultured cells. In the APP/PS1 mouse model of AD, Jiaotaiwan alleviates AD-related lipid deposition and dysregulation by activating AMPK and modulating the downstream lipogenic effectors, providing also protective effects on the blood-brain barrier and neural cells.

title: [Aerobic exercise improves metabolic disorders and multi-organ damage in diabetic rats by activating the Sirt1/Creb1/Ppargc1a axis].
journal: Nan fang yi ke da xue xue bao = Journal of Southern Medical University
abstract: To investigate the effects of aerobic exercise and exhaustive anaerobic exercise on organ glucose metabolism and function in type 2 diabetic rats and the underlying mechanisms. Forty male SD rats were randomly divided into normal control group (n=10) and diabetic model group (n=30). In the latter group, type 2 diabetes was induced by high-fat and high-sugar diet combined with streptozotocin injection. The diabetic rat models were further assigned to diabetic control, aerobic exercise and exhaustive anaerobic exercise groups (n=10) with an 8-week exercise intervention. General physiological indicators of the rats were measured, and liver, quadriceps, heart and prefrontal cortex tissues were collected for HE, Masson, PAS staining and immunohistochemistry. Hepatic expression of key metabolic enzymes and genes were detected using Western blotting and qPCR. Compared with the normal control rats, the diabetic rats had significantly increased body weight, liver index, fasting blood glucose and serum levels of metabolic markers with severe hepatic steatosis, fibrosis, glycogen loss, skeletal and cardiac muscle damages, and downregulated DRD1/DRD5, 5-HT and TH in the prefrontal cortex. Aerobic exercise markedly reversed these abnormalities, alleviated organ pathological lesions, suppressed hepatic G6PC and glycolytic enzymes, upregulated Sirt1 mRNA, and restored cortical neurotransmitter-related proteins in the diabetic rats. Exhaustive anaerobic exercise lowered body weight and fasting glucose of the diabetic rats, but caused significant increase of serum metabolic indicators, worsened hepatic steatosis and tissue fibrosis, reduced glycogen, and further reduction of neurotransmitter expressions in the brain. Aerobic exercise protects organ function of diabetic rats by regulating glucose-lipid metabolism, relieving inflammation and fibrosis and improving neurotransmitter function, while exhaustive anaerobic exercise can aggravate metabolic disorders and cause tissue damage.

title: [40 Hz flicker light stimulation suppresses STING signaling to improve cognitive dysfunction in mice with Parkinson disease].
journal: Nan fang yi ke da xue xue bao = Journal of Southern Medical University
abstract: To explore the effects of 40 Hz flicker light stimulation on cognitive dysfunction in mice with subacute Parkinson disease (PD) induced by 1-methyl-4-phenyl-1,2,3,6-tetrahydropyridine (MPTP) and the underlying mechanisms. Forty 8-week-old male C57BL/6 mice were randomly allocated to a control group and 4 MPTP-induced PD model groups receiving blank treatment, 40 Hz flicker light stimulation, or stereotactic intraventricular injection of a control AAV (sh-NC) or an AVV carrying sh-STING. After the treatments, the mice were examined for changes in motor functions and cognitive behaviors. Immunofluorescence staining, Nissl staining, ELISA, Western blotting and RT-qPCR were used to detect hippocampal co-localization of S100A10 and C3 with GFAP, Nissl neuron count, serum interleukins, and nigral and hippocampal expressions of α-syn, TH, synaptic, astrocytic, inflammatory, SOCS3, JAK2-STAT3, and the STING pathway at the mRNA and protein levels. The PD mouse models exhibited impaired motor and cognitive functions with lowered TH and elevated α‑syn expressions. 40 Hz light flicker stimulation improved cognitive function of the PD mice, significantly increased the number of hippocampal neurons and S100A10 expression, and reduced the expressions of p-STING/STING, C3, GFAP, IL-6, and TNF‑α. Compared with the PD mice with sh-NC injection, the mice receiving sh-STING AVV injection showed significantly improved cognitive function with lowered hippocampal expression level of C3 and increased expression of S100A10 without significant changes in the expression levels of SOCS3 and JAK2-STAT3. 40 Hz flicker light stimulation mitigates impairment of cognitive function in mice with MPTP-induced PD by inhibiting STING overactivation to promote A2 astrocyte polarization and enhance hippocampal synaptic plasticity.

title: Are the Mental Health Concerns of Youth Presenting to an Emergency Department More Scute or Severe than Those Waiting for Outpatient Care?
abstract: BackgroundMental health patients presenting to the emergency department (ED) are potentially more unwell than those waiting for mental health services on outpatient waitlists. They often receive prioritized mental health follow up care, yet this practice may be unjustified if they do not have greater severity and acuity of mental illness.ObjectiveAdolescent mental health patients from an outpatient waitlist sample are compared to those who attended the ED to seek help but were not admitted to hospital.MethodAdolescents completed intake questionnaires at time of outpatient (regular or post ED) intake visit at a pediatric hospital in Canada. Statistical comparisons between the groups were completed on multiple measures of demographic and clinical features.ResultsThe ED group reported more substance use, higher psychiatric symptom severity scores for ODD, ADHD, and MDD, more recent self-harm, suicidal ideations and suicide attempts and lower general functioning. They also reported more ethnic diversity.ConclusionThe greatest differences were seen on measures of suicide risk acuity and substance use, which suggests outpatient interventions immanently focussed on these targets for ED attenders. Considering the high amount of suicide risk, despite lower acuity, in the outpatient wait list sample, future studies should investigate how to most equitably service these two populations.

title: Human cytochrome P450 27A1-a variety of reactions, applications, and potentials for drug targeting.
journal: Drug metabolism and disposition: the biological fate of chemicals
abstract: The human cytochrome P450 (P450) 27A1 enzyme is most often described as a liver enzyme that initiates the alternative (acidic) pathway of bile acid synthesis. Although this is certainly an important role for this enzyme, research has shown that it has a significantly wider role to play in normal physiology and disease pathology. This minireview aims to provide a useful reference for studies showing the many ways P450 27A1 is involved in human health and to help researchers access useful methods. The distribution, expression, and regulation of the enzyme in both normal and disease states are discussed. A catalog of steady-state kinetics experiments is included. A review of methods for recombinant expression, inhibition, and studying redox partner interactions is also included. Two key examples of connections to disease, breast cancer and neurodegeneration, are explored as possible applications of P450 27A1 research and illustrations of the complexity of the role of the enzyme. Finally, a few key areas of needed clarification are suggested with hopes to inspire researchers to contribute to work in this important area. SIGNIFICANCE STATEMENT: Human cytochrome P450 27A1 and its products, particularly 27-hydroxycholesterol, are increasingly connected to variety of diseases such as cerebrotendinous xanthomatosis, atherosclerosis, multiple cancers, and neurodegenerative diseases. This review explores the systemic physiological control and basic enzymology of cytochrome P450 27A1 to facilitate collaboration across these different biomedical dimensions toward advancing diagnosis and treatment.

title: Autoimmune encephalitis and paraneoplastic neurological syndrome: A practical guide for clinicians.
abstract: Autoimmune encephalitis and paraneoplastic neurological syndromes comprise a group of disorders affecting both the central and peripheral nervous systems, with an increasing incidence likely attributable to increased clinical awareness and continuous advances in diagnostic methods. These conditions are characterized by an aberrant immune response and often require the involvement of multiple specialties, including neurology, pediatrics, oncology, immunology, and intensive care medicine. In this review, we aimed to provide clinicians with essential knowledge for recognizing clinical syndromes suggestive of these entities, thereby facilitating the establishment of an appropriate diagnostic and therapeutic approach.

title: Reduced social brain coupling to others' face threats in narcissism.
abstract: Although several studies have linked narcissism to reduced empathy, the neural mechanisms underlying narcissistic behavior in socially complex, naturalistic contexts remain poorly understood. This study investigated how grandiose narcissistic traits are associated with neural dynamics in empathy-related areas of the "social brain" when participants observed another person receiving face-threatening feedback. We hypothesized that individuals with high narcissistic traits would exhibit lower intersubject correlation (ISC), indicating less synchronized neural responses across participants, in the anterior insula (aINS), dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (dlPFC), and posterior cingulate cortex (PCC) in response to face threats directed at others. Participants with high (n = 28) and low (n = 30) scores in grandiose narcissism watched videos during functional magnetic resonance imaging in which another person received face-threatening feedback to a personal story. Consistent with our hypothesis, highly narcissistic individuals exhibited reduced ISC in the dlPFC and PCC. In aINS, the effect did not reach statistical significance. The present findings suggest that trait narcissism reduces convergence in empathic responses particularly in areas related to cognitive empathy when witnessing social threats targeted at others. These findings further indicate that ecologically relevant experimental designs may help clarify how personality traits are expressed in neural responses to socially meaningful events.

title: Analytical Performance of the Sysmex XF-1600 Flow Cytometer in Routine Clinical Practice.
abstract: Flow cytometry systems are increasingly used for the identification and quantification of lymphocyte subpopulations, supporting the diagnosis and monitoring of hematological and immunological conditions. This study aimed to evaluate the analytical performance of the novel Sysmex XF-1600 flow cytometer for lymphocyte subpopulation quantification in peripheral blood, including precision, carryover, and agreement with established laboratory methods. Peripheral blood samples from routine clinical workload were analysed in the hematology laboratory. Analytical performance was assessed by evaluating precision (repeatability and reproducibility) and carryover. Absolute lymphocyte and leukocyte counts obtained using the XF-1600 automated sample preparation and volumetric counting system were compared with the Sysmex XN-series hematology analyser, while lymphocyte subset quantification was compared with the Navios flow cytometer (Beckman Coulter). The XF-1600 showed coefficients of variation below 6% for major lymphocyte populations, including CD3+, CD4+, CD8+, CD19+, and CD16+/CD56+ cells. No carryover was detected. Comparison with the Sysmex XN analyser showed strong correlation for leukocyte and lymphocyte counts (Spearman's ρ = 0.986 and 0.993, respectively). Comparison with the Navios flow cytometer demonstrated high correlation across lymphocyte subpopulations (Spearman's ρ > 0.9 for most parameters). Bland-Altman and Passing-Bablok analyses showed good agreement between methods, although some parameters were not fully interchangeable. The Sysmex XF-1600 flow cytometer demonstrated good analytical performance for lymphocyte subset quantification, with high precision and strong agreement with routinely used laboratory methods. The integration of automated sample preparation and volumetric counting may support standardization of immunophenotyping workflows in clinical laboratories.

title: Neurocognitive characteristics of perceptual feedback processing differ in autism.
journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
abstract: Autistic individuals often show reduced adaptation to changing environmental demands, but the neurocognitive mechanisms underlying this difference remain unclear. We asked whether it may be explained by reduced sensitivity to external feedback and changes in task difficulty. Autistic and non-autistic adults of either sex, matched for cognitive ability, performed a pitch discrimination task in which their response was immediately followed by feedback. Accuracy was similar between the two groups, yet autistic participants exhibited a markedly reduced feedback-related negativity (FRN), an event-related EEG potential differentiating explicit negative versus positive feedback. They also showed weaker modulation of feedback-evoked EEG responses by perceptual difficulty. Lastly, they showed reduced trial-by-trial behavioral updating of perceptual bias following recent correct and easy trials. These effects were replicated in a follow-up experiment conducted 1-2 years later. When combined they classified autistic and non-autistic participants with about 80% accuracy. Together, our findings indicate that multiple processes for evaluating perceptual decisions and adjusting subsequent behavior differ in autism and likely contribute to slow updating in changing contexts.Significance Statement Autism is associated with reduced adaptation to changing environments in both behavior and neural signals, but the underlying neurocognitive mechanisms remain unclear. Here, we show that autistic individuals exhibit a reduced feedback-related negativity (FRN), an EEG component that is present when receiving negative instead of positive feedback. They also show weaker neural modulation by perceptual difficulty and reduced trial-by-trial behavioral updating of perceptual bias following recent correct and easy trials. These effects were replicated in a follow-up study. When combined, they classified autistic and non-autistic participants with high accuracy. These findings suggest that reduced flexibility in autism is associated with reduced processing of external feedback and task difficulty.

title: One-shot learning of paired association navigation with biologically plausible schemas.
journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
abstract: After learning a multiple paired-association (MPA) navigation task, rodents can rapidly learn new cue-location associations after a single exposure, a phenomenon proposed to be facilitated by cognitive schemas. However, it remains unclear what schemas support this behavior and how they could be implemented in biological neural circuits. Here, we identify a set of schemas sufficient for gradual then one-shot paired-association navigation, and implement them in a fully neural agent using biologically plausible plasticity rules. The agent gradually acquires a low-dimensional spatial metric representation using a path-integration based temporal-difference error, enabling self-localization across different environments. It also contains a memory network that forms one-shot associations between sensory cues and goal locations, implemented using reward-modulated exploratory Hebbian (EH) plasticity. A third network performs vector subtraction between the agent's current and goal location to compute goal-directed actions. Supplementing these schemas with an actor-critic enables one-shot navigation past obstacles. Lastly, learning a working-memory gating mechanism using the temporal-difference error enables one-shot learning even with brief cue and distractor presentation. The model reproduces key behavioral features of rodent learning in the MPA task and generates testable predictions about the neural mechanisms underlying schema-based one-shot learning.Significance Statement Schema-dependent learning is exemplified by better recall of a lecture when one already has a schema for understanding. A rodent navigation task showing a shift from slow to rapid learning has been proposed to reflect such schema use, yet how schemas are neurally implemented and enable faster learning is poorly understood. We clarify this gap in this computational study by describing several schemas and implement them as neural networks with biologically plausible learning rules. Composing them into an agent reproduces schema-dependent rodent learning behavior. Because schemas also shape self beliefs, clarifying their neural basis has implications for psychopathology. At the same time, understanding how biological schemas support rapid learning may inform advances in machine learning.

title: Emotional Content Enhances Attentional Tracking of Conversations through Context-Sensitive Modulation of Auditory-Language Networks.
journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
abstract: Engagement in conversation often requires continuous monitoring of relevant speech in a continuously evolving auditory environment. Emotional salience of semantic content may influence this process, but its role in attentional tracking of continuous speech remains unclear. We address this question using an audiovisual "Cocktail-party" paradigm combined with source-localized magnetoencephalography and encoding-decoding analyses. Participants (18 female, 14 male) selectively attended to one dialogue while ignoring a concurrent distractor dialogue, with both emotional salience and semantic coherence of the conversations manipulated independently. Decoding analyses revealed that negatively valenced, high-arousal, and socially relevant semantic content strengthened neural speech tracking, but only for attended dialogues. This effect depended on semantic structure, emerging earlier in semantically coherent than incoherent dialogues. Encoding analyses further showed latency- and region-specific effects across temporal, parietal, and frontal cortical regions. Emotional salience and coherence jointly modulated mid-latency (100 - 250 ms) responses, whereas late-latency (270 - 450 ms) responses were driven primarily by emotional salience. These findings demonstrate that emotional meaning enhances neural prioritization of attended speech and semantic coherence shapes the temporal dynamics of this enhancement. Together, these results indicate context-sensitive emotional modulation of auditory-language processing during selective listening of continuous speech.Significance Statement Understanding how the brain prioritizes and selectively processes information in naturalistic, continuously evolving audiovisual scenes such as conversations is a central challenge in neuroscience. Here, we show that conversations conveying negatively valenced, high-arousal, and socially relevant content enhance neural tracking of attended speech in a noisy cocktail-party setting. This enhanced tracking depends on the semantic structure of the conversation, emerging earlier for coherent dialogues that are easy to follow. Furthermore, we show that emotional content strengthens mechanisms related to speech comprehension and sharpens segregation of relevant from irrelevant talk. These findings demonstrate that emotional meaning and semantic continuity jointly shape cortical processing of continuous speech, providing new insight into how the brain selects and processes meaningful information during a conversation.

title: Object detection through dynamic motor-sensory convergence in freely moving rats.
journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
abstract: To detect objects in natural environments, animals must coordinate movement and sensation. This process unfolds dynamically, as perceivers actively shape sensory input through ongoing motor actions in a closed loop. In this study, we use precise tracking of behavioral kinematics to investigate the initial phase of object interaction, asking: what motor-sensory strategies support object detection during natural approach? Using high-speed videography and advanced tracking tools, we tracked whisker and head dynamics as male rats approached and contacted objects. We found that whisker-object interactions converged toward a distinct ratio between changes in whisker angle and curvature, denoted [Formula: see text] In a motor-sensory phase plane this ratio appears as a line, reflecting a regime in which small motor adjustments produce large curvature changes during contact. This motor-sensory ratio cannot stabilize during free-air whisking and thus can serve as a signature for object presence. Rats gradually converged toward this object-dependent mechanical signature across contacts, and proximity to [Formula: see text] predicted subsequent head movements and the termination of object approach. Convergence to [Formula: see text] was invariant to object shape and texture and to whisker's length. Moreover, touch-induced pumps both signaled and reinforced convergence. The results suggest that rats use successful convergence to this object-dependent motor-sensory contingency as a signature of object presence. Object detection thus emerges as a closed-loop dynamical process in which action, mechanics, and sensation jointly shape perceptual inference.Significance Statement How does a rat know it is touching an object with its moving whiskers? We trained freely moving rats to discriminate objects while tracking whisker kinematics at high resolution. We found that the detection phase involved whisker-object interactions that converged toward a distinct ratio between changes in whisker angle and curvature. This ratio can arise mechanically only when whiskers contact an external object, making its attainment a reliable indication of object presence. During object approach, rats steered their exploratory movements to seek this motor-sensory contingency, marking the transition to focused exploration or disengagement. These findings reveal a dynamical, closed-loop mechanism for object detection in freely moving rats.

title: Evaluation of virtual care services offered to children across Ontario, Canada, during the COVID-19 pandemic.
Analysis of Muscle Fibre Orientation in the Human Medial and Lateral Pterygoid Muscles Using Diffusion Tensor Imaging: A Methodological Study.
abstract: Deep anatomical locations limit functional and morphological evaluation of the medial and lateral pterygoid muscles, which are vital for mandibular kinematics. The lateral pterygoid comprises superior and inferior heads with distinct anatomical and functional characteristics. Diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) tractography non-invasively visualises in vivo muscle fibre orientation. This methodological study aimed to quantify 3D fibre orientation of the medial pterygoid and both lateral pterygoid heads using DTI tractography, comparing simulated mandibular rest and 25-mm open-mouth positions. Healthy males (28.4 ± 4.6 years) underwent cephalometric radiography and 3.0-T MRI. T1-weighted and DTI sequences were acquired at both mandibular positions. Target muscles were segmented. MRtrix3 tractograms were reconstructed (fibre orientation distribution [FOD] amplitude cutoffs: 0.02-0.10). Fibre orientations, quantified via vector projection onto coronal and sagittal planes, were statistically compared. Tractography successfully visualised fibre orientation; optimal FOD amplitude cutoffs varied among individuals and muscles. The medial pterygoid showed no significant changes. During mouth opening, seven participants exhibited marked fibre reorientation in the superior head and seven in the inferior head, although the direction and magnitude varied among participants. However, group-level analyses revealed no significant orientation differences for any muscle. DTI tractography enabled in vivo evaluation of medial and lateral pterygoid internal fibre architecture. Between simulated rest and 25-mm open-mouth positions, group-level differences were non-significant in either plane despite variable lateral pterygoid reorientation. Inter-individual variability and FOD cutoff dependence highlight the need for participant- and muscle-specific parameter adjustment. These findings provide a methodological basis for future DTI applications in temporomandibular disorders and masticatory dysfunction.

title: Associations between Simple and Complex Executive Function skills and adaptive function in a sample of 3-year-olds enriched for variation in autism and ADHD traits.
journal: Journal of child psychology and psychiatry, and allied disciplines
abstract: Adaptive Functioning-including communication, socialization, and daily living skills-predicts outcomes and quality of life for individuals who are autistic or have ADHD, yet its cognitive underpinnings in early development remain poorly understood. Executive Functions (EFs) are a plausible mechanism linking developmental level or IQ to Adaptive Functioning, but prior work in preschoolers has relied largely on parent-reported EF measures, which are vulnerable to shared method variance with parent-reported Adaptive Functioning. Here, we examine associations between performance-based EF and parent-reported Adaptive Functioning among 3-year-olds enriched for variation in autism and ADHD traits. One hundred and twenty-nine children (109 with a family history of autism and/or ADHD) completed six EF tasks, reduced through factor analysis to scores for Simple EF (pertaining to simple response inhibition, holding information in mind, and applying a rule) and Complex EF (involving complex response inhibition, shifting response in accordance with a new task set, and updating information). Adaptive Functioning was assessed using the Vineland Adaptive Behavior Scales-Second Edition. Autism traits, ADHD traits and developmental level were measured using the SRS-2, CBCL-Preschool, and MSEL, respectively. Hierarchical regression models tested whether each EF index was positively associated with Adaptive Functioning, and whether these effects remained after controlling for developmental level, autism traits, and ADHD traits. Both Simple and Complex EF were positively associated with Adaptive Functioning (β = .293, .316). While associations between Simple EF and Adaptive Functioning were accounted for by general developmental level, Complex EF showed associations with Adaptive Functioning above and beyond developmental level, autism, and ADHD traits. EFs in general, and Complex EF in particular, represent a promising, developmentally-sensitive target for early support in the toddler or preschool years, which could positively impact the day-to-day functioning of children with a family history of autism/ADHD, or already showing elevated autism traits.

title: Understanding epistemic injustice among individuals with psychotic experiences: a scoping review protocol.
Bridging the Divide: A Call to Integrate Perinatal and Infant Mental Health.
journal: Journal of the American Academy of Child and Adolescent Psychiatry

title: Individualized brain mapping for neurosurgical planning.
abstract: The need for personalised approaches in neurosurgery arises from marked variations in the distribution and performance of functional networks among individual brains. Functional MRI and diffusion tractography have been widely adopted for neurosurgical planning. However, the way in which neuroimaging results are used clinically remains largely qualitative. This review explores how personalised neurosurgical mapping can move toward quantitative, patient-specific predictions by adopting techniques from the field of neuroscience. Exciting potential comes from extending our largely static measures of network organisation with metrics probing the dynamic nature of information processing in the brain. Such multidimensional approaches show promise to capture aspects of complex behaviour relevant to everyday function beyond the mainstream focus on language and motor skills. Yet, translation of advanced approaches into the clinic faces many challenges. Progress will require validated metrics capturing individually-unique patient profiles, methods for robust multimodal integration, clinically usable analytical tools, and outcomes that better capture real-life performance. By combining spatial, structural and temporal features of brain networks, neuroimaging may evolve from a 'localisation' tool into a platform for personalised neurosurgical prediction, intervention and longitudinal care.

title: A Sensorimotor-Interoceptive Model for Sensory Phenomena in Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder: Neural and Computational Mechanisms.
abstract: Classical models of obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) grounded in cognitive-affective processes do not fully account for sensory phenomena (SP), including bodily discomfort, incompleteness, and not-just-right experiences that often precede or accompany compulsive behavior. To address this gap, we propose a sensorimotor-interoceptive model for the sources, generation, and maintenance of SP and SP-driven compulsions in OCD. Specifically, the posterior insula may integrate external sensory signals with internal bodily signals within the perceptual module. These integrated signals are subsequently processed by the salience module centered on the anterior insula and anterior cingulate cortex, where heightened error monitoring may assign excessive salience to integrated signals and recruit the supplementary motor area and primary motor cortex to initiate corrective actions. Dysfunction of a cerebellum-centered forward system may then produce persistent mismatches between predicted and actual action outcomes, which are re-entered into the perceptual module and sustain a recurrent feedback loop. The framework therefore conceptualizes SP-driven compulsions as maladaptive attempts to resolve persistent sensory errors. Predictive coding and active inference provide a computational account of these processes. We underscore that this sensorimotor-interoceptive model, intended to complement existing models, provides an account of symptoms in which SP are prominent and may therefore contribute to a more comprehensive understanding of OCD.

title: Diaphragm reserve utilisation in motor neurone disease: a novel ultrasound-derived physiological index.
abstract: Respiratory involvement is a major determinant of prognosis in motor neurone disease (MND; or amyotrophic lateral sclerosis), yet conventional static respiratory measures provide limited information about how much available diaphragm thickening capacity is recruited during quiet breathing. We evaluated diaphragm reserve utilisation (RU), an ultrasound-derived ratio of tidal diaphragm thickening relative to maximal diaphragm thickening, as a novel physiological descriptor in MND. In a prospective observational study, 38 patients with MND and 20 healthy controls underwent right hemidiaphragm ultrasound to measure thickness at end-tidal expiration, peak tidal inspiration and peak maximal inspiration. Thickening fractions and RU were calculated. Between-group differences in diaphragm ultrasound indices were assessed. Secondary analyses examined relationships between RU, respiratory function and survival. Tidal diaphragm thickening fraction was similar between patients with MND and controls, whereas maximal thickening fraction was lower in MND, resulting in higher RU in MND than controls. This pattern indicates that patients with MND maintained tidal diaphragm thickening while using a greater proportion of their available maximal thickening capacity. Higher RU was also associated with shorter survival, supporting its potential physiological and clinical relevance. Diaphragm reserve utilisation describes the proportion of measured diaphragm thickening capacity recruited during tidal breathing. Patients with MND demonstrated preserved tidal thickening despite reduced maximal thickening capacity, resulting in higher RU than healthy controls. This supports RU as a novel physiological index of relative diaphragm thickening reserve utilisation. The relationship between RU and survival warrants validation in larger prospective cohorts.

title: Sex-Related Multivariate Organization of Glymphatic MRI Markers in Healthy Adults.
abstract: Sex may influence MRI-derived markers related to brain fluid and perivascular processes, but sex differences across glymphatic-related MRI markers remain unclear. We investigated sex differences in individual and multivariate glymphatic-related MRI markers in healthy adults. The Human Connectome Project (HCP) was used as the discovery dataset (n = 971; 521 females), and the Chinese Human Connectome Project (CHCP) was used as an independent validation dataset (n = 307; 157 females), from which a range of glymphatic-related MRI markers was derived. Sex differences in these glymphatic-related markers were examined, followed by principal component analysis (PCA) to characterize their multivariate organization. We found that males showed higher choroid plexus volume fraction, perivascular space volume fraction, and white-matter free-water fraction, but lower values for the index of diffusivity along the perivascular space and the index of periventricular diffusivity than females. PCA identified two dominant components explaining 63.45% of the total variance. Most glymphatic-related MRI markers showed consistent sex-related patterns in CHCP, and sex differences in HCP-projected component scores were directionally consistent with HCP. PCA performed separately in HCP and CHCP showed high similarity of the retained two-dimensional subspaces, with differences in individual component loading patterns. Together, these findings characterize sex-related variation in glymphatic-related MRI phenotypes at the individual-marker and multivariate levels.

title: Should athletes take omega-3 supplements? Current evidence for recovery, adaptation and performance.
journal: Current opinion in clinical nutrition and metabolic care
abstract: To evaluate whether long-chain n-3 polyunsaturated fatty acid supplementation provides meaningful benefits for recovery, training adaptation or performance in athletic populations, while distinguishing mechanistic plausibility from demonstrated functional effects. Recent data from athletic populations show that Omega-3 Index (O3I) values commonly fall below proposed cardioprotective thresholds, although athlete-specific targets remain unvalidated. Meta-analyses and controlled trials suggest that supplementation may modestly reduce muscle soreness and attenuate selected losses of muscle function following damaging exercise. However, findings are inconsistent across formulations, doses and outcomes, and benefits do not translate reliably into improved strength, endurance, power or sport performance. Evidence concerning female, masters and contact-sport athletes is limited. Routine supplementation cannot at present be recommended for all athletes. Targeted supplementation may be considered following dietary and, wherever appropriate, biomarker assessment, while recognizing that benefits during unusually damaging or congested training remain unproven.

title: The influence of caregivers' lived experiences in decision-making processes on care transitions in young-onset dementia.
abstract: BackgroundCaregivers of people with young-onset dementia (YOD) hold diverse perspectives on the caregiving trajectory, reflecting the heterogeneity of underlying etiologies and the life stages of these people, who are often in the midst of employment, child-rearing, and other social responsibilities. Post-diagnostic care and services are often suboptimal and caregivers tend to be hesitant to initiate formal care and support services.
