We refer to movements of persons between different levels of care or physical locations as care transitions.ObjectiveTo improve caregiver support, this study aimed to provide insights into caregivers' perspectives on the decision-making process regarding care transitions and associated barriers and facilitators.MethodsSeventeen interviews with six caregivers of people with YOD were analyzed. Inductive content analysis was used to generate codes, followed by constant comparative analysis to create categories and themes describing caregivers' experiences.ResultsBarriers and facilitators influencing the decision-making process related to the initiation of care transitions were identified at two themes: individual and contextual level. Six categories and 23 sub-categories emerged. Individual-level categories included the character traits of the caregiver, the caregiver's need for support, impacts on the quality of the caregiver's relationship, and the burden experienced by the caregiver. Contextual-level categories included the social environment and the caregivers' experiences with healthcare professionals.ConclusionsCaregivers' decision-making regarding care transitions is shaped by thinking processes, character traits and contextual aspects. Healthcare professionals should strengthen collaboration and communication with caregivers. Acknowledging grief and supporting caregivers'sense of control are essential to providing adequate support.

title: [Sulfide balneotherapy as a promising approach to the prevention and treatment of cognitive impairments (literature review).].
abstract: Currently, there are no specific treatments for cognitive disorders, although some therapies can delay their development in the early stages. Despite this, medical research continues to explore, develop, and implement new methods for the prevention and treatment of cognitive disorders. Until recently, hydrogen sulfide gas was not considered scientifically significant, as it was not believed to have physiological importance. Instead, it was primarily viewed as a poison. However, in the past 20 years, the synthesis of hydrogen sulfide in central nervous system cells has been established, and its important regulatory role in the chemical mechanisms of cell-to-cell signaling has been proven. The inclusion of hydrogen sulfide in the group of gasotransmitters, which are short-lived gaseous signaling molecules that perform various biological functions in mammals, has led to a renewed interest in it. Over the past decade, numerous approaches to the therapeutic use of hydrogen sulfide have been developed, either by donating it or by inhibiting its biosynthesis. Hydrogen sulfide donors are substances that can release hydrogen sulfide in response to specific stimuli. Sulfide mineral water is a natural exogenous donor of hydrogen sulfide. This is evidenced by the results of recent experimental and clinical studies. Hydrogen sulfide is related to the development of certain neuropsychiatric conditions, which are based on impaired neuroplasticity of the central nervous system due to insufficient endogenous production.

title: [Prospects of application of peptide preparations in therapy of Alzheimer's disease.].
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a serious kind of pathology that mainly affects older adults and significantly reduces the quality of their life. Despite decades of research, the pathogenesis of AD, the causes and the trigger mechanism of its occurrence remain the subject of debate. This review examines hypotheses of the pathogenesis of AD, including the involvement of amyloid-β peptide and hyperphosphorylated tau protein fragments in neuroinflammation and neurodegeneration. It also discusses potential therapies for AD based on peptides that target various aspects of the disease's pathogenesis.

title: Vitamin C and Methylprednisolone Modulate Apoptotic and Transcript Responses in a B-35 Scratch Screening Model.
abstract: In vitro mechanical injury platforms using proliferative neuronal cell lines provide accessible systems for preliminary pharmacological screening before progression to differentiated, primary, or in vivo models. We investigated the effects of vitamin C and methylprednisolone, alone or in combination, on cell viability, Annexin V/PI-defined apoptotic cell death, scratch-gap closure, and selected transcript responses in the B-35 rat neuroblastoma cell line. Mechanical injury was induced in confluent B-35 monolayers using a standardized scratch method. Vitamin C, methylprednisolone, or their combination was applied either immediately after injury (0 h) or after a 24 h delay. Scratch-gap closure was quantified by image-based analysis, and IL-4, IL-10, and TUBB3 expression was evaluated by quantitative real-time PCR. Early combined exposure to vitamin C and methylprednisolone was associated with low apoptotic cell fractions, faster scratch-gap closure, and higher IL-4, IL-10, and TUBB3 mRNA levels than either single treatment, whereas delayed treatment showed attenuated responses. These findings describe treatment-associated changes in a simplified B-35 cell-line screening model. They should not be interpreted as evidence of regeneration, pharmacological synergy, neuroprotection, or spinal cord injury therapy. Protein-level validation, proliferation control, and confirmation in differentiated neuronal cultures, primary neuronglia co-cultures, organoid or slice models, and in vivo injury systems are required before mechanistic or translational conclusions can be drawn.

title: Arcuate kisspeptin neurons display two types of calcium events: Regulation by sex, gonads, and senktide.
abstract: The pattern of gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) release controls reproduction in vertebrates and is regulated by feedback from the gonads. Evidence is accumulating that steroid-sensitive hypothalamic arcuate kisspeptin-neurokinin B-dynorphin (KNDy) neurons drive GnRH pulses. KNDy neurons exhibit coordinated, large amplitude calcium signals in vivo that precede LH pulses; coordinated events persist in brain slice recordings of these cells. We used cre-lox to target GCaMP6f expression to KNDy neurons. Brain slice calcium imaging was done to identify putative unitary calcium events. Newly devised analyses identified two types of calcium events (fast and slow) in intact and gonadectomized male and female adult mice. Neurokinin B and the neurokinin-3 receptor agonist senktide are strong activators of action potential firing in KNDy neurons. The effect of senktide on calcium events over 5-min baseline and treatment periods was determined. Gonadectomy unexpectedly increased GCaMP6f fluorescence; illumination levels were adjusted to standardize initial levels. Senktide increased the frequency of fast and slow events; this effect was enhanced in gonadectomized mice for fast events. Senktide increased fast event amplitude only in gonadectomized mice. For slow events, in contrast, senktide increased amplitude in all groups, with the increase being larger in gonadectomized than intact mice. Differential regulation by gonadectomy and senktide modulation of fast and slow events suggests two separate mechanisms for these events, which likely also differ from the large amplitude events observed in vivo in KNDy neurons.

title: Neurophysiological and Behavioural Effects of Combined Cannabis Concentrates and Alcohol Among People Who Regularly Use Alcohol and Cannabis.
abstract: Increasingly potent concentrated cannabis products containing high levels of Δ9-tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) are being consumed with alcohol. This combination is known to acutely impair cognitive and psychomotor abilities, although few studies have evaluated alcohol and cannabis co-use using neural measures. This naturalistic feasibility study explored the acute effects of co-intoxication on behavioural performance and brain activity, measured via electroencephalography (EEG), during a performance monitoring task administered three times over a 4.5-h period. Participants (N = 17, 65% male) were heavy drinking community members (age M = 31.7 years; SD = 10.27) who regularly use cannabis. EEG was recorded while participants completed a speeded visual-flanker task at baseline (sober) before consuming a standardized dose of alcohol and a cannabis concentrate product, followed by EEG recordings 1-h (intoxicated) and 4-h post co-consumption (recovery). Recordings were processed to obtain six event-related potential components: the stimulus-locked N1, P2, N2 and P3 and response-locked error-related negativity (ERN) and error positivity (Pe). Repeated measures ANOVAs revealed that behavioural measures at the intoxicated timepoint showed an increase in errors (p < 0.005; η2 p = 0.35) and significant decrease in response time (RT) (p < 0.001; η2 p = 0.50) compared to sober and recovery periods. Measures of brain activity also demonstrated significant change across time with largest amplitudes when sober, smaller amplitudes when intoxicated, then an increase in amplitude to near sober levels at recovery for stimulus-locked (P2, N2 and P3) and response-locked components (ERN and Pe). Thus, compared to sober and recovery periods, the behaviour at the intoxicated timepoint revealed significantly greater impulsivity (RT) leading to significantly higher error rates, while measures of cognitive processing (i.e., decision-making, error detection, performance monitoring/adaptation) showed significantly diminished levels of brain activity. Performance and neurophysiology measures remained diminished at recovery compared to baseline. Understanding neurocognitive functioning during co-intoxication may provide insights into specific cognitive processes that may impact function in everyday activities such as driving. Trial Registration: NCT06259916.

title: Effectiveness of rimegepant across multiple acute migraine attacks: A real-world, prospective, multicentric study.
journal: Cephalalgia : an international journal of headache
abstract: AimRimegepant is an effective acute migraine treatment, with limited evidence regarding its consistency across multiple migraine attacks. The primary aim is to assess rimegepant effectiveness across multiple migraine attacks.MethodsIn this real-world, prospective, multicentric study we assessed participants who treated up to four different migraine attacks with rimegepant 75 mg orally disintegrating tablet. Data was collected every 30 min from migraine onset up to 2 h post dose using an electronic diary. Our primary outcome was 2-h pain freedom across all-treated attacks; secondary outcomes were: consistency of response (percentage of participants who achieved 2-h pain freedom in at least two treated attacks), safety and tolerability.ResultsWe enrolled 191 participants (80.1% females, age 44.8 [43.2-46.5] years, disease duration 28.4 [25.0-31.8] years, 27.7% with chronic migraine, 9.6 [8.9-10.9] baseline monthly migraine days-MMDs). We collected data from 377 migraine attacks (191 first-treated, 110 s-treated, 46 third-treated and 30 fourth-treated). Two-hour pain freedom was achieved in 44.6% (168/377) of treated attacks [39.3-49.6]. After correction for age, timing of rimegepant intake, baseline pain intensity, ongoing preventive treatment, and number of preventive drug classes that previously proved ineffective, 2-h pain freedom was associated with female sex (odds ratio (OR) = 2.3 [1.2-4.3], p = 0.012), no ongoing mAbs treatment (OR = 3.2 [1.6-6.4], p = 0.001), and lower MMDs (OR = 1.05 [1.0-1.1], p = 0.002). Consistency of response was 36.4% [27.3-45.5] (40/110). Participants reporting at least one adverse event were 11.5% (22/191).ConclusionOur study confirms the effectiveness of rimegepant in nearly half of treated attacks and describe the consistency of response in a relatively large real-world population where one out of five participants achieved 2-h pain freedom in all-treated migraine attacks. No new safety signals were identified.

title: Predicting health-related quality of life among older patients: an external validation of the Health Assessment Tool (HAT) in Swedish primary care.
abstract: As populations age, primary care (PC) requires tools that capture multidimensional health and patient-centred outcomes. Health-related quality of life (HRQoL) is a key indicator of well-being in older adults but is rarely used to evaluate the predictive performance of geriatric assessment tools. We aimed to externally validate the Health Assessment Tool (HAT) in Swedish PC by examining its ability to discriminate between HRQoL levels at baseline and predict changes over time. This multicentre prospective cohort study included 1005 adults aged ≥60 years from six Swedish PC centres (November 2022-December 2024). HAT scores were derived from five indicators: personal and instrumental activities of daily living, gait speed, cognitive function and number of chronic diseases. HRQoL was measured using EuroQol 5-Dimension 5-Level questionnaire (EQ-5D-5L) and EuroQol Visual Analogue Scale (EQ-VAS) at baseline and 6-12 months' follow-up. Predictive performance was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) values for both cross-sectional HRQoL levels and clinically meaningful changes over time. The HAT demonstrated moderate to good predictive performance across HRQoL outcomes. Cross-sectional AUCs ranged from 0.80 to 0.81 for EQ-5D-5L (10th and 15th percentiles) and 0.71-0.74 for EQ-VAS (25th and 40th percentiles). For longitudinal improvements, AUCs were lower for predicting 10% and 15% increases in EQ-5D-5L (0.69-0.74). In contrast, HAT showed moderate to good predictive capacity for 25% and 40% increases in EQ-VAS (0.71-0.80). HAT consistently outperformed its individual components. The HAT shows predictive validity for HRQoL in older PC patients. Its integration into routine assessments may support the early identification of patients with poor HRQoL and more personalised care planning.

title: [Synergistic regulation of neuro-tumor interactions by ultrasound and biomaterials].
journal: Zhong nan da xue xue bao. Yi xue ban = Journal of Central South University. Medical sciences
abstract: The peripheral nervous system plays an important role in remodeling the tumor microenvironment (TME) and promoting malignant progression through the release of neurotransmitters and neuropeptides, regulation of immune cell function, and remodeling of the neural microenvironment. However, conventional strategies such as surgical denervation and pharmacological blockade are limited by poor specificity, irreversible injury, and systemic adverse effects. Ultrasound neuromodulation, as a noninvasive and controllable physical intervention, provides a novel technical approach for the dynamic regulation of peripheral nerve activity. This review first systematically summarizes the functional mechanisms by which autonomic nerves, sensory nerves, and Schwann cells (SCs) regulate tumors, and then describes how low-intensity pulsed ultrasound (LIPUS) and low-intensity focused ultrasound (LIFU) remodel the TME by modulating ion channel activity, neurotransmitter release, and SC plasticity. Recent advances in ultrasound-responsive piezoelectric nanomaterials and molecular delivery systems are further discussed, including strategies to enhance acoustic signal transduction, enable controlled release of neuroactive molecules, and improve the precision of neuromodulation. Ultrasound neuromodulation can effectively modulate peripheral nerve function, and its integration with ultrasound-responsive biomaterials may enhance targeting precision, demonstrating potential for application in cancer therapy.

title: RBM15/IGF2BP1-mediated m6A methylation of AKR1B10 promotes the progression of cervical squamous cell carcinoma.
journal: Zhong nan da xue xue bao. Yi xue ban = Journal of Central South University. Medical sciences
abstract: RNA-binding motif protein 15 (RBM15) is a methyltransferase involved in N6-methyladenosine (m6A) modification and has been shown to be associated with the initiation and progression of various malignancies. This study aims to investigate the biological function and underlying mechanism by which RBM15 promotes the progression of cervical squamous cell carcinoma (CSCC) through in vitro and in vivo experiments. The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) and Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) databases were used to analyze differences in the mRNA expression levels of RBM15, aldo-keto reductase family 1 member B10 (AKR1B10), and insulin-like growth factor 2 mRNA-binding protein 1 (IGF2BP1) between CSCC and adjacent non-tumor tissues, as well as the associations of RBM15, AKR1B10, and IGF2BP1 expression with overall survival in patients with CSCC. Real-time PCR and Western blotting (WB) were used to determine the expression levels of RBM15, AKR1B10, and IGF2BP1 in CSCC tissues and adjacent normal tissues. Cell Counting Kit-8 (CCK-8), colony formation, 5-ethynyl-2'-deoxyuridine (EdU) staining, wound-healing, and Transwell migration and invasion assays were performed to investigate the effects of RBM15 knockdown on the proliferation, migration, and invasion of CSCC cells. A nude mouse xenograft model was established to evaluate the effect of RBM15 knockdown on tumor growth. Methylated RNA immunoprecipitation (MeRIP) was performed to assess m6A modification of AKR1B10. RNA immunoprecipitation (RIP) and actinomycin D assays were used to analyze the interactions of RBM15 and IGF2BP1 with AKR1B10 mRNA. Small interfering RNAs (siRNAs), including si-IGF2BP1 and si-YTHDF1, were used to knock down IGF2BP1 or YTH N6-methyladenosine RNA-binding protein F1 (YTHDF1), respectively, and their roles in regulating AKR1B10 mRNA stability were analyzed. Analysis of TCGA and GEO data showed that the mRNA and protein expression levels of RBM15, AKR1B10, and IGF2BP1 were significantly up-regulated in CSCC tissues (all P0.05). RBM15-mediated m6A modification promotes CSCC progression through the IGF2BP1-AKR1B10 axis. RBM15 may serve as a potential biomarker for predicting outcomes in patients with CSCC.

title: The Cost-Of-Living Crisis and Suicide Rates.
abstract: Background: The cost-of-living crisis may be contributing to suicide rates, but this has not been adequately tested. Aims: We aimed to determine whether the cost-of-living crisis is associated with suicide rates in multiple countries and areas-within-countries. Method: We sourced country- and area-within-country-level monthly suicide data at a minimum from January 1, 2019, to December 31, 2022 (and at a maximum from January 1, 2016, to June 30, 2023), and population denominator and monthly headline consumer price index (CPI) data. We calculated the yearly change in inflation as the percentage change in CPI for one month versus the equivalent month in the previous year. We estimated associations between yearly change in inflation (lagged by one month) and suicide rates for each country and area-within-country, using autoregressive negative binomial regression. We summarized results using weighted means. Results: We obtained data on 1,372,994 suicides from 54 countries. At the country-level, for every 1.0% increase in yearly inflation in the previous month, there was an average 0.2% increase in suicide rates. The association was strongest in those aged 30-49 and 50-69; for every 1.0% increase in yearly inflation in the previous month, there were 0.3% and 0.6% increases in suicide rates for these age-groups, respectively. This pattern held for males in these age-groups, with increases of the same magnitude, and for females aged 50-69, with a 0.8% increase. At the area-within-country-level, the picture was even starker. Limitations: Study limitations include: the ecological design; the single measure of inflation; potential variations in suicide data quality; lack of representation by low-and-middle-income countries (LMICS); lack of availability of sex, age and sex/age breakdowns for some countries and areas-within-countries; and potential issues with multiple testing. Conclusions: There is an association between the cost-of-living crisis and suicide rates internationally. Public and social policies that improve people's circumstances are critical.

title: Pathology of the intervertebral disks and other spinal lesions in 31 aging inbred mouse strains.
abstract: In a large-scale aging study of 31 inbred strains of mice, a variety of age-related lesions arose in and around the spine (vertebrae, spinal cord, and adjacent connective and muscle tissues), including lesions of intervertebral disks, vertebrae, muscles, soft tissues, nerves, ganglia, and spinal cord that were either sporadic or strain-specific. In most cases, the mice did not present with obvious clinical signs, as many lesions were mild. Lesions included herniated or displaced intervertebral disk fragments, which appeared to be sporadic in most strains but were common in others. Fibro-osseous lesions of bones were a systemic disease in female mice with no effect on disk disease. Rhabdomyosarcomas were common in A/J mice surrounding the vertebrae but also invaded into the spinal canal, sometimes almost transecting the cord. Lymphomas affected all AKR/J mice, sometimes infiltrating into the spinal canal. Muscular dystrophy of the musculature surrounding the spine, due to mutations in the dysferlin (Dysf) gene, was common in A/J and SJL/J mice. Coccygeal hemivertebra was a novel strain-specific lesion only in PL/J mice. Sporadic lesions in and around the spine included hemangiosarcomas, lymphomas (both enlarged lymph nodes and invading in and around the vertebrae), schwannomas, histiocytic sarcomas, poorly differentiated sarcomas, and epidermoid/dermoid cysts. Since these strains have all been sequenced and annotated, polymorphisms in genes known to affect the pathogenesis of some of these lesions will be reported in other publications.

title: Cutaneous Mast Cells Contribute to the Analgesic Effect of Manual Therapy on CCD Rats.
abstract: Lumbar disc herniation (LDH) commonly induces low back and leg pain. Manual therapy (MT) is effective in relieving such pain clinically, but its mechanism remains unclear. Given that acupoint regions are enriched with mast cells that respond to mechanical stimulation, this study explored whether MT alleviates CCD-evoked neuropathic pain and its association with the modulation of cutaneous mast cells. Sprague-Dawley (SD) rats were randomized into sham, chronic compression of dorsal root ganglion (CCD), MT, and mast cell inhibition (MCI) groups. After CCD modeling, MT was administered at BL57 starting on day 4 for 14 days, while MCI received acupoint cromolyn sodium injection. Paw withdrawal threshold (PWT) was measured. Mast cell activation was assessed using immunofluorescence and toluidine blue staining. Calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP), substance P (SP), Piezo1, and Piezo2 were determined via immunofluorescence; inflammatory cytokines and neurotransmitters by ELISA; expression of MAPK, Piezo1, and Piezo2 by qRT-PCR. MAPK expressions were also detected by Western blot. CCD reduced PWT from day 3, whereas MT significantly restored PWT from day 11. In skin, CCD increased mast cell activation, CGRP, SP, tumor necrosis factor (TNF)-α, interleukin (IL)-6, IL-1β, 5-hydroxytryptamine (5-HT), and histamine (HA), all of which were attenuated by both interventions. In DRG, CCD elevated p-ERK, p-JNK, and p-p38 MAPK without altering total MAPK expression, and both interventions suppressed MAPK phosphorylation. Piezo2 was upregulated in CCD and reduced by MT and MCI in both tissues. In skin, Piezo1 remained unchanged, while in DRG, CCD downregulated Piezo1 significantly. MT can relieve CCD-induced mechanical allodynia, an effect associated with inhibited cutaneous mast cell activation, attenuated peripheral neuroinflammation, and reduced MAPK hyperphosphorylation in the DRG.

title: Muscular = Fake? Testing a Picture-Word Pairing Procedure to Increase Muscle Appearance Satisfaction in Young Men.
journal: European eating disorders review : the journal of the Eating Disorders Association
abstract: When men compare their bodies to those of muscular fitness models, this may result in dissatisfaction with their own muscularity. We tested whether pairing pictures of male muscular-ideal models with synonyms of 'fake' results in an increase in muscle satisfaction and a decrease in self-objectification among young men. Male participants (N = 66, M age = 22.86, SD = 2.14) were randomly assigned to an experimental (n = 32) or control (n = 34) condition of a picture-word pairing procedure. Both conditions showed the same pictures of muscular-ideal models. In the experimental condition these pictures were systemically paired with synonyms of 'fake'; in the control condition these pictures were randomly paired with words related to sports and colours. Participants in the experimental condition showed a modest increase in muscle appearance satisfaction from pre- to posttest whereas control participants did not change. Change in muscle appearance satisfaction was not moderated by internalisation of the appearance ideal. The predicted decrease in self-objectification was not found. The present research provides initial evidence that pairing pictures of male muscular-ideal models with 'fake' can enhance muscle appearance satisfaction in young men. The study was pre-registered at https://aspredicted.org/uy9zp5.pdf.

title: Synthetic Insights on Donepezil: An Anti-Alzheimer Drug.
abstract: Alzheimer's disease is a severe condition that poses significant global health concerns to international health agencies and remains a major threat to public health. As there is no cure for Alzheimer's disease, various anti-Alzheimer's medications are used to manage its symptoms. Donepezil is one of the most highly marketed drugs, known for its positive effects on cognition, function, behaviour and overall patient condition, making it a standout treatment option. Various synthetic methods have been developed to produce more efficient pathways that minimise by-products and maximise yield. This review summarises the reported literature on various synthetic routes for producing Donepezil. We have also made an effort to highlight the advantages and limitations of prior literature, which may lead to potential improvements for future research. This work will serve as a foundation for upcoming researchers, ultimately benefiting the well-being of Alzheimer's patients and human society as a whole.

title: Comparison of the Safety and Efficacy of Remimazolam for Sedation in Adults Undergoing Fiberoptic Bronchoscopy: A Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
abstract: Fiberoptic bronchoscopy requires effective sedation to ensure patient comfort while preserving gas exchange, hemodynamic stability, and predictable recovery. Remimazolam, a novel ultra-short-acting benzodiazepine, has emerged as a potential alternative to traditional sedatives. However, its safety and efficacy compared with those of other sedatives remain under investigation. This meta-analysis evaluated the safety and efficacy of remimazolam versus dexmedetomidine, midazolam, and propofol in adults undergoing fiberoptic bronchoscopy. A systematic review of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) was conducted using 5 databases through January 2026. Outcomes included respiratory depression, hypotension, bradycardia, time to target sedation depth, procedure success rate, emergence time, and postanesthesia care unit (PACU) stay. Relative risks (RR) or mean differences (MD) with 95% CI were calculated using a random-effects model. Sixteen RCTs (2325 patients) were included. Remimazolam significantly reduced respiratory depression (RR: 0.51, 95% CI: 0.36-0.73, P<0.001), hypotension (RR: 0.50, 95% CI: 0.34-0.73, P<0.001), and bradycardia (RR: 0.37, 95% CI: 0.22-0.65, P=0.001) versus controls. Sedation onset was faster than dexmedetomidine (MD: -2.19 min), but slower than propofol (MD: 0.49 min). Success rates were comparable across groups (RR: 1.12, 95% CI: 0.98-1.28, P=0.097). Compared with dexmedetomidine and midazolam, remimazolam shortened emergence (MD: -1.79 and -4.37 min, respectively) and PACU stay (MD: -3.58 and -6.70 min). Remimazolam provides effective sedation for fiberoptic bronchoscopy with advantages in terms of respiratory and hemodynamic safety, rapid recovery, and procedural efficiency.

title: Beyond the hype: why artificial intelligence is not a shortcut to solving mental illness.
abstract: More than one billion people worldwide live with a mental health disorder, and rising prevalence continues to outpace the capacity of mental health services. Artificial intelligence, and large language models in particular, have been widely proposed as a remedy. Nevertheless, psychiatry's limited mechanistic understanding of illness processes (compounded by their psychosocial roots) and its reliance on largely subjective clinical assessments limit what any artificial intelligence model can achieve. We examine where artificial intelligence genuinely helps, including large multimodal data-sets and administrative tools such as ambient scribes, and where evidence for direct therapeutic use remains preliminary and safety concerns are real. We also highlight risks posed by artificial intelligence to the research process itself, from hallucinated citations to unverifiable analysis pipelines. Ultimately, whether artificial intelligence comes to augment psychiatric care or hollow it out depends less on model capability than on the choices of stakeholders and policymakers.

title: Short-term outcomes, longer-term disability and relapse risk in LGI1-antibody encephalitis.
abstract: Leucine-rich glioma-inactivated-1 antibody encephalitis (LGI1-Ab-E) is a common and immunotherapy-responsive form of encephalitis. However, it is not known which immunotherapy regimens improve short-term outcomes, longer-term disability and relapse risk. Further, it is not known if the widely-utilised modified Rankin Scale (mRS) accurately captures quality of life (QoL) in LGI1-Ab-E, complicating disability measurements and interpretation of immunotherapy responses. A multicentre, international, real-world comparative analysis of patients with LGI1-Ab-E. Retrospective data from patient records evaluated short-term seizure and cognitive outcomes, 1-6 year disability, and future relapse risk associations, by integrating demographics, clinical features investigations and exposures to immunotherapies and antiseizure medications (ASMs). Patient- and neurologist-rated QoL assessments were used to establish an evidence-based mRS threshold for defining clinically significant disability. Cox proportional hazard models, Anderson-Gill, and generalised linear mixed-effects models were employed. 181 patients were included, with median age at onset 63 years (range 23 - 92); 122/181 (67%) were male. Short-term outcomes, evaluated at both five and ten weeks post-treatment initiation, identified exposure to immunotherapies associated with seizure resolution (OR = 13.97, 95%CI = 6.10-32.01; p < 0.0001 and OR = 8.53, 95%CI = 4.14-17.55; p < 0.0001, respectively), notably with corticosteroids, plasma exchange and rituximab, but not ASMs, intravenous immunoglobulins or steroid sparing agents. Conversely, seizure recurrence was observed after discontinuation of oral prednisolone, but not other immunotherapies or ASMs (OR = 39.53, 95%CI = 12.70-122.20, p < 0.0001). To evaluate longer-term disability, first, mRS scores were calibrated using QoL assessments: this identified a significant increase in patient-rated disability at mRS score of 2. Hence, using mRS 0-1 as a favourable outcome, we identified worse mRS at nadir associated with greater one-year disability (OR = 2.56, 95%CI = 1.56-4.20, p = 0.0003), and each month of delayed immunotherapy associated with a 16% increased risk of disability (HR = 1.16, 95%CI = 1.06-1.35, p = 0.004). Additionally, absence of immunotherapy associated both with greater one-year disability (OR = 5.67; 95% CI 1.19-26.54, p = 0.03) and a relapsing course (OR = 7.64, 95%CI = 2.51-21.77, p = 0.0002). Both a relapsing course, observed in 38% of patients, and the number of relapses associated with step-wise worsening of disability and QoL-outcomes. Rituximab exposure was the only identified clinical factor associated with reduced future relapse risk, by 93% (HR = 0.07, 95%CI = 0.01-0.48, p = 0.002). Persistent serum LGI1-IgMs, but not LGI1-IgGs, at one-year, associated with future relapses (HR = 11.69, 95%CI = 1.58-145.80, p = 0.02). Distinctive clinical factors and select immunotherapies, particularly intravenous methylprednisolone and plasma exchange, but not ASMs, associated with favourable short-term outcomes, patient-centric longer-term disability and relapses in LGI1-Ab-E. Our findings provide evidence-based disability thresholds, highlight novel prognostic biomarkers, and pragmatically guide LGI1-Ab-E care, pending randomized clinical trials.

title: Intestinal Methanogen Overgrowth in Parkinson's Disease Reflects Constipation Physiology: A Matched Cohort Study.
abstract: Intestinal methanogen overgrowth (IMO) is associated with delayed intestinal transit. Chronic constipation and slow colonic transit are common in Parkinson's disease (PD) and may favor methanogen overgrowth. The goal was to characterize IMO prevalence in PD and compare findings with constipation reference groups. We retrospectively studied patients with PD who underwent hydrogen-methane breath testing at a tertiary center. IMO was defined as peak methane ≥10 ppm. Patients were matched 1:2 to constipation-spectrum comparators by age, sex, body mass index, test substrate, and irritable bowel syndrome status. A separate constipation cohort with objective colonic transit data provided sensitivity comparisons. Among 93 patients with PD, IMO was present in 46.2% and small intestinal bacterial overgrowth (SIBO) in 15.1%. Isolated IMO occurred in 36.6% and IMO + SIBO in 9.7%. IMO prevalence did not differ by substrate, time relative to PD diagnosis or Movement Disorder Society Unified Parkinson's Disease Rating Scale part III motor score (all P > 0.05). IMO prevalence was comparable between PD and the matched chronic constipation population (42.1% vs. 44.7%; P = 0.703) with similar methane burden. Specifically, IMO prevalence in PD was comparable to that in slow-transit constipation (46% vs. 48%), but significantly higher than in normal-transit constipation (46% vs. 29%; adjusted P = 0.038). In this first characterization of IMO in PD, nearly half of patients tested met criteria for IMO-a prevalence comparable to slow-transit constipation and independent of motor severity or disease duration. Prospective studies should determine whether constipation-directed treatment alone or with methanogen-directed therapy improves outcomes in this population.

title: Regular Exercise Moderates Age-Related Cognitive Differences in Midlife Women: Domain-Specific Effects on Processing Speed and Working Memory.
journal: Medicine and science in sports and exercise
abstract: This study examined whether regular exercise moderates age-related cognitive differences in midlife women, including reaction time (RT), executive planning, and working memory. We further investigated whether these effects differ across exercise modalities. This cross-sectional study included ninety-three women (35-63 years) who completed simple RT, working memory, and executive planning tasks. Participants were categorized by exercise regularity and modality. Time-based outcomes were analyzed via Linear Mixed Models; accuracy via Generalized Estimating Equations. Pairwise comparisons utilized Welch's t-tests with FDR correction. Regular exercise moderated age-related slowing in simple RT (β=-3.083, p=0.032). Resistance training participants exhibited faster RTs than those in the non- regular exerciser, aerobic, and other exercise groups. Regarding working memory, the impact of exercise on response speed was significantly moderated by both age and task difficulty (β = -15.91, p < 0.001). Specifically, exercise-related benefits became more pronounced as cognitive load increased, a trend primarily driven by older participants, whereas these effects were less evident in younger cohorts. However, no modality-specific differences were observed. In contrast, executive planning performance was associated with age, with no significant effects of exercise or exercise-related interactions. These findings suggest that regular exercise moderates age-related cognitive differences in midlife women, particularly in processing speed and high-demand working memory. These benefits were domain-specific: modality-specific advantages emerged in simple reaction time, whereas working memory benefits were modality-independent. The notable efficacy of resistance training further highlights the importance of exercise modality. Findings identify midlife as a sensitive window for targeted exercise interventions to preserve cognitive health.

title: Focused Ultrasound for Essential Tremor in Denmark: Results After 1 Year of Follow-Up.
journal: Movement disorders : official journal of the Movement Disorder Society
abstract: Essential tremor (ET) is the most common hyperkinetic movement disorder. Magnetic resonance-guided focused ultrasound thalamotomy (MRgFUSTh) has become an established therapy in drug-refractory tremor as one treatment option. Here, we present the results of a large cohort of MRgFUSTh-treated ET patients followed-up 1 year post-ablation. The primary endpoint durability of tremor reduction at 12 months at this timepoint. This was a single-hospital cohort study. Prior to, and 12 months after, treatment, patients were rated according to the Fahn-Tolosa-Marin (FTM) scale, Quality of Life in Essential Tremor (QUEST) scale, Patient Global Assessment of Change (PGIC), as well as general health, well-being, and factors relating to social and everyday activities. Finally, side effects and adverse event data were collected at 12 months. The current cohort comprised 111 patients. Patients showed good response to MRgFUSTh with a mean decrease of 29.5 points in the total FTM-score from pretreatment (95% CI: 26.3; 32.8, P < 0.0001) corresponding to 62.4% (95% CI: 56.4%; 68.5%). This meant a reduction in the FTM-score of 13.8 points (± 5.2 points, 95% CI: 12.79; 14.73, P < 0.00001) or 85.2% (±24.2%, 95% CI: 80.70%; 89.78%) in the treated limb. For QUEST, symptoms improved by 20.9 points (95% CI: 12.1; 29.6, P < 0.0001) corresponding to a relative improvement of 54% (95% CI: 33.2%; 75.5%). Results showed clear and persistent tremor improvements as assessed by both clinicians and patients. © 2026 The Author(s).
