title: Connexin and Pannexin Channels in Traumatic Spinal Cord Injury: Mechanisms of Secondary Injury and Therapeutic Opportunities.
abstract: Traumatic spinal cord injury (tSCI) causes immediate mechanical damage followed by a secondary cascade of excitotoxic, oxidative, metabolic, and inflammatory events that expands tissue loss. Connexin (Cx) and pannexin (Panx) channels are increasingly recognized as potential amplifiers of this secondary injury. This focused review summarizes the structural and biophysical properties of these channels that are relevant to the injured spinal cord, their cellular localization, and the experimental evidence linking Cx43 and Panx1 activity to ATP release, calcium dysregulation, neuroinflammation, tissue loss, neuropathic pain, and functional recovery after tSCI. We also review genetic and pharmacologic studies of channel inhibition and discuss the limited but emerging evidence for Cx-mediated signaling in paralyzed skeletal muscle. Evidence is strongest for astrocytic Cx43 hemichannels, whereas the contribution of Panx1 after tSCI remains promising but less completely defined. Throughout, we distinguish findings demonstrated directly after tSCI from mechanisms inferred from other tissues or disease models and identify priorities for translational research.

title: Atopic dermatitis.
journal: JAAPA : official journal of the American Academy of Physician Assistants
abstract: Atopic dermatitis (AD) is a chronic, relapsing inflammatory skin disease that commonly begins in childhood and can persist or first appear in adulthood. Its burden reflects pruritus, sleep loss, pain, infection, psychosocial effects, and treatment demands rather than visible extent alone. Diagnosis is clinical and requires recognition of age- and skin tone-specific morphology and exclusion of mimics. AD management begins with moisturization, gentle bathing, topical anti-inflammatory therapy, education, and proactive maintenance. Newer nonsteroidal topical agents and targeted systemic therapies have expanded options, but treatment should be individualized according to age, disease severity and control, comorbidities, safety, access, and patient preference. Routine elimination diets, topical antimicrobials for uninfected disease, antihistamines as primary antipruritic therapy, and systemic corticosteroids are generally not recommended for AD. This review provides physician associates with a practical approach to diagnosis, severity assessment, stepwise treatment, complication recognition, and timely referral.

title: Repeated Head Impacts May Compromise White Matter Integrity and Bimanual Coordination in American Football Players.
abstract: Repeated head impacts (RHI) in American Football may contribute to subtle white matter (WM) abnormalities and functional deficits even in the absence of clinically diagnosed concussion. Contact athletes would demonstrate tract-specific differences in fractional anisotropy (FA) and mean diffusivity (MD) compared with noncontact controls, and high-exposure (HE) athletes would show greater within-season diffusion change, worse bimanual coordination, and greater symptom burden than low-exposure (LE) athletes. Prospective cohort study. Level 3. Twenty-two male varsity American Football players and 13 male noncontact controls underwent preseason diffusion tensor imaging. Football athletes were monitored over a single season using helmet-mounted accelerometers and stratified into HE and LE groups. Tract-specific FA and MD were derived using probabilistic tractography. Pre-post SCAT3 symptom and severity checklist data were collected from all football athletes, and pre-post Kinarm Ball-on-Bar (BOB) bimanual coordination data were available for 12 athletes. At preseason, contact athletes demonstrated higher FA in 15 of 16 tracts compared with noncontact controls, with lower FA in the forceps minor. MD was lower in 10 of 16 tracts, higher in the bilateral inferior longitudinal fasciculus, and similar in the corticospinal tract and superior thalamic radiation. Over the season, HE athletes sustained more impacts (P 0.99), and SCAT3 symptom and severity scores remained low with no meaningful between-group differences. In 22 contact athletes, repeated head-impact exposure was associated with preseason WM differences and worsening bimanual coordination across a single season, while longitudinal tract-level DTI and symptom-based clinical measures showed limited between-group change. Objective motor assessment and advanced neuroimaging may help characterize subtle consequences of RHIs that are missed by routine symptom-based tools.

title: Phase 3 randomized trial of latozinemab in frontotemporal dementia due to GRN mutations.
journal: Alzheimer's & dementia : the journal of the Alzheimer's Association
abstract: Heterozygous progranulin gene mutations causing frontotemporal dementia (FTD-GRN) are associated with deficiency in progranulin (PGRN). Latozinemab is a human monoclonal immunoglobulin G1 (IgG1) antibody designed to elevate PGRN levels in people with heterozygous loss-of-function (LOF) GRN mutations. A pivotal phase 3 trial, INFRONT-3 (NCT04374136), evaluated the efficacy, safety, and biomarker changes of 60 mg/kg of intravenously administered latozinemab or placebo every 4 weeks for 96 weeks in participants who have or are at risk for FTD due to heterozygous LOF GRN mutations. Those completing the double-blind phase could enter a 96-week open-label safety extension. Although latozinemab administration resulted in sustained elevation of plasma and CSF PGRN concentrations in symptomatic participants with FTD-GRN (primary analysis population), there was no treatment-related slowing of disease progression as measured by clinical or biomarker assessments. No adverse safety signals were identified. INFRONT-3 provides the first phase 3 efficacy and safety results for an investigational therapy in FTD-GRN.

title: CNTN2 Deficiency Disrupts Ascending Auditory Neuroglial Interactions and Redox Homeostasis in Neural Presbycusis.
abstract: Neural presbycusis disrupts auditory timing and speech perception, yet its molecular basis remains poorly understood. This study identifies Cntn2 as the Ranvier's nodal molecule significantly downregulated in aged auditory nerves. Cntn2 heterozygous knockout (Cntn2+/-) mice showed elevated auditory brainstem response thresholds and prolonged wave latencies and interpeak intervals, whereas distortion product otoacoustic emission thresholds were largely preserved. Hair cell and ribbon synapses were preserved, with no obvious ultrastructural changes, suggesting that overt hair cell loss or synaptic structural loss is unlikely to be the main cause of the early phenotype. Instead, transmission electron microscopy revealed myelin outfoldings and aberrant node of Ranvier morphology in myelinated auditory nerve fibers, accompanied by increased Schwann cell density. Multiplex immunofluorescence and Western blot analysis showed disruption of nodal molecular organization along the ascending auditory pathway from cochlea to auditory cortex. Transcriptomic profiling and oxidative stress assays further linked CNTN2 deficiency to altered neuroglial interaction and redox imbalance. Early unilateral AAV-mediated CNTN2 restoration partially improved threshold and latency abnormalities. These findings identify CNTN2-dependent neuroglial integrity as an important contributor to auditory conduction of neural presbycusis and may provide a new direction for future therapeutic studies.

title: The Human Anatomy and Physiology Society, Anatomical Donor Stewardship Committee thematic issue on best practices and skills for gross anatomy instructors and faculty.
Real-world clinical, biomarker, and imaging outcomes of lecanemab in Alzheimer's disease: a multicenter longitudinal cohort study in Jiangsu, China.
journal: Alzheimer's & dementia : the journal of the Alzheimer's Association
abstract: Real-world data on lecanemab's efficacy and the longitudinal dynamics of plasma biomarkers are scarce in Chinese patients with Alzheimer's disease (AD). In this multicenter cohort study, 181 AD patients received biweekly lecanemab. Disease-stage-specific Clinical Dementia Rating-Sum of Boxes meaningful within-patient change defined response at Months 3, 6, and 12. We used penalized models, receiver operating characteristic analysis, attrition comparisons, and exploratory Month 3 plasma biomarker analysis. Cognitive response emerged at Month 6 and intensified by Month 12, largely restricted to mild cognitive impairment and mild dementia due to AD. Repeated five-fold cross-validated areas under the curve across the follow-up timepoints were 0.560, 0.747, and 0.773, with apolipoprotein E ε4 positivity and more severe cognitive impairment linked to lower response odds. Plasma phosphorylated tau 217 (p-tau217) and amyloid beta (Aβ) 42/40 altered as early as Month 3. Month 3 Aβ42/40 showed modest exploratory discrimination. The incidence of amyloid-related imaging abnormalities was 7.2%, all asymptomatic. Lecanemab is effective and safe in AD over 6 to 12 months. Early biomarker changes (p-tau217, Aβ42/40) precede clinical improvement, serving as scalable response indicators.

title: Brains for dementia research at 18: Commitment to impact the value of human post-mortem tissue.
journal: Alzheimer's & dementia : the journal of the Alzheimer's Association
abstract: The Brains for Dementia Research (BDR) project was established to provide high quality, neuropathologically characterized post-mortem brain tissue from a cohort of participants longitudinally assessed for outcomes that are relevant for research in relation to dementia. From its origins in 2008, over 3200 individuals with and without dementia consented to participate in the project and to donate their brains after death. Now, 18 years later over half of these pledges have been collected. Here we celebrate the BDR project and provide an update on its contributions to the field of dementia research thus far, and the future promise of maximizing benefit from this endeavor with the conception of the "BDR Collaborative". The BDR Collaborative seeks to align and intersect data generated on this cohort and to accelerate advances in our understanding of neurodegeneration.

title: A scoping review of psychosocial functioning in young people with personality pathology: current evidence and methodological issues.
journal: Borderline personality disorder and emotion dysregulation
abstract: Despite evidence that personality pathology often emerges during the transition from adolescence to adulthood and leads to lasting psychosocial impairment, research on how these impairments manifest and develop in young people remains limited. This review aims to map existing literature on psychosocial functioning in individuals aged 12-25 with clinical or subclinical personality pathology, examining definitions and measures of functioning, its relationship with personality pathology, and the impact of early interventions, while identifying gaps for future research. A total of 37 studies were included: 14 cross-sectional, 7 longitudinal, and 16 on early interventions. In clinical samples, overall functioning was most assessed, whereas community studies focused on specific domains. Across studies, adolescents with personality pathology showed greater psychosocial impairment than both healthy controls and other psychopathology groups, both cross-sectionally and prospectively. Improvement in global psychosocial functioning has been documented across varying interventions but there was the lack of differences between treatment approaches. While emerging evidence highlights psychosocial dysfunction in young people with personality pathology, methodological limitations hinder comparisons across studies. Developmentally appropriate, culturally sensitive, and domain-specific assessments are needed to track psychosocial impairment alongside symptom progression in young people.

title: Nanoparticles and their significant risks: a comprehensive review of toxicological and regulatory perspectives.
abstract: Nanoparticles are increasingly important as drug carriers due to their ability to enhance solubility, stability, and selective delivery of therapeutic agents, enabling accumulation at disease sites, interaction with cell-surface receptors, and penetration of biological barriers such as the blood-brain barrier. Despite these numerous advantages, their potential toxicity remains a key obstacle to safe clinical use. Emerging evidence suggests that nanoparticles may alter the composition of the gut microbiome, potentially affecting metabolism, immune homeostasis, neurobehavioral pathways, and reproductive function by influencing hormonal regulation and fertility. This review provides a detailed analysis of the toxicological aspects of nanoparticles, including cytotoxicity, oxidative stress, potential genotoxicity, and effects on immune responses such as inflammation and immunosuppression. In vivo biodistribution, organ accumulation, and effects on liver enzymes are also discussed, emphasizing the role of the liver in drug metabolism and the potential risk of impaired detoxification. Additionally, the review examines the effects of nanoparticles on the gut microbiome and reproductive system. It emphasizes their capacity to disrupt the microbial balance, the intestinal barrier integrity, and reproductive hormone homeostasis. We discuss regulatory issues for nanotechnology-based medicinal products, emphasizing the importance of standardized testing protocols and long-term safety assessments. Finally, future perspectives and developmental directions for nanoparticles have been highlighted. This review highlights the need for a comprehensive understanding of nanoparticle toxicity mechanisms, which is crucial for their safe design and further development in nano-based therapy.

title: Neuropsychological profiles and behavioural correlates in individuals exposed to repetitive head impacts: findings from the NEwTON study.
abstract: Repetitive head impacts (RHI) are associated with an increased risk of neurodegenerative disease, most notably chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE). This study characterized neuropsychological profiles of RHI-exposed individuals compared to unexposed controls. To investigate whether cognitive dysfunction is linked to behavioural symptoms in RHI, we examined associations between executive functioning, social cognition and behavioural disinhibition. We included RHI-exposed individuals (N = 72, 90.4% male, mean age 53.84 ± 12.45) and unexposed, cognitively healthy controls (N = 40, 82.5% male, mean age 54.55 ± 12.12) from the "Neurodegeneration: Traumatic brain injury as the Origin of Neuropathology" (NEwTON) study from Amsterdam UMC. Neurocognitive functioning was assessed through a comprehensive test battery covering episodic memory, attention and processing speed, executive functioning, visuospatial abilities, language and semantic memory, and social cognition. Behavioural disinhibition was measured in the RHI group using informant-based questionnaires (the positive items of the Frontal Behavioural Inventory (FBI) and the Neuropsychiatric Inventory (NPI)). Group differences in cognitive domains were assessed with analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) corrected for age, sex and education. The RHI-exposed group was evaluated for Traumatic Encephalopathy Syndrome (TES) criteria (No TES, Suggestive of CTE, Possible CTE, Probable CTE), TES subgroups were exploratively compared on cognitive performance. Associations between behavioural disinhibition and executive functioning or social cognition were assessed with regression analyses. RHI-exposed individuals performed worse on episodic memory (η2 = 0.12, pFDR ≤ .001), language and semantic memory (η2 = 0.10, pFDR = .001), executive functioning (η2 = 0.04, pFDR = .046), and social cognition (η2 = 0.04, pFDR = .040). No differences were found for visuospatial abilities (η2 = 0.01, pFDR = .221) and, although borderline significant, attention and processing speed (η2 = 0.03, pFDR = .074). Greater TES severity was associated with poorer performance on all cognitive domains. No significant associations were found between executive function or social cognition and behavioural disinhibition, as measured with the NPI and the FBI positive subscale (all p > .05). RHI-exposed individuals showed poorer cognitive performance across several domains (episodic memory, executive functioning, social cognition and language and semantic memory). We found no association between cognitive function and behavioural disinhibition. Further longitudinal studies employing neuroimaging and biomarker data are needed to disentangle the underlying pathology in populations at risk for CTE.

title: Comparative characterization of OncoPro™ and Wnt-based media reveals distinct phenotypic and pharmacologic states in patient-derived tumor organoids.
abstract: Patient-derived tumor organoids (PDTOs) are strongly influenced by culture medium. We compared OncoPro™ (OP) Tumoroid Culture medium with conventional Wnt/R-spondin/noggin (Wnt) medium. This recently developed OP medium offers a standardized, serum-free alternative to Wnt-based formulations. We compared OP and Wnt media across 36 PDTO lines from various malignancies (colorectal, pancreatic, breast, lung, gastric, gastroesophageal junction, biliary head and neck and unknown primary), assessing establishment success. Selected PDTO models were subjected to downstream characterization, including morphological assessment and bulk transcriptomic profiling with comparison to public single-cell RNA sequencing reference datasets (n = 11), whole-exome sequencing (WES) (n = 9), and pharmacological response profiling to a 33-drug panel (n = 3). Adaptation from Wnt medium to OP succeeded in 83.3% (15/18), whereas de novo establishment favored Wnt (33.3% vs 11.1%). Key oncogenic driver alterations were retained across matched organoid cultures, supporting preservation of tumor-relevant genomic features. Transcriptomic profiling confirmed preserved tumor-identity across media, while revealing different epithelial state programs: Wnt upregulated proliferation/stemness-associated genes (e.g. LGR5) and OP enriched adhesion-associated genes and inflammatory/TGF-β programs. In scRNA databases OP signatures preferentially mapped to malignant epithelial compartments in pancreatic cancer, whereas Wnt signatures were linked to non-malignant epithelium. Similarly, in colon cancer OP signature mapped predominantly to the malignant epithelial compartments. Drug (n = 33) screening in pancreatic- and colorectal cancer PDTOs (n = 3) demonstrated consistent medium-dependent shifts: Wnt-grown PDTOs were globally more sensitive in the screened subset, particularly to MAPK-axis inhibitors and apoptosis-sensitizers, while OP-grown PDTOs exhibited relative resistance. Culture medium composition is a key determinant of PDTO phenotype, transcriptome and drug sensitivity. Wnt medium was associated with drug-sensitive states, whereas OP medium was associated with adhesion- and inflammatory-related programs, relative resistance in the screened subset of 33 drugs and closer alignment with malignant epithelial programs in the analyzed pancreatic / colorectal cancer single-cell atlases.

title: Optimal strategy for treatment of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease-comparison of clopidogrel-based antiplatelet agent treatment versus aspirin plus low dose rivaroxaban therapy (OACART study): a study protocol for a multicenter, open-label, randomized, non-inferiority trial.
abstract: Recent studies have demonstrated the superior benefits of clopidogrel compared to aspirin in reducing mortality, myocardial infarction, stroke, and hospitalization in chronic stable patients with coronary stenting. Furthermore, dual pathway inhibition by combining low-dose rivaroxaban with aspirin (DPI) has shown superior effects in preventing cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, and stroke in stable atherosclerotic patients. However, no studies have directly compared these treatment strategies in the same population. This randomized controlled trial aims to compare clopidogrel-based antiplatelet therapy with or without aspirin (CAPT) to DPI in a 1:1 ratio in patients with high-risk coronary artery disease (CAD) or in patients with both CAD and peripheral artery disease (PAD). Optimal strategy for treatment of Atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease-comparison of Clopidogrel-based Antiplatelet agent treatment versus aspirin plus low dose Rivaroxaban Therapy (OACART) trial is a randomized multi-center study comparing the performance of the maintaining CAPT or DPI in a 1:1 ratio. The trial is powered for the non-inferiority of the CAPT in patients with chronic stable high-risk CAD or CAD+PAD to DPI with respect to the primary and secondary efficacy endpoints at 36 months. Between November 2023 and April 2026, we will recruit 2758 participants from multi-center in Korea, and we will examine the net clinical outcome, including all-cause death, any myocardial infarction, any stroke, any ischemia-driven revascularization (CAD or PAD), acute limb ischemia, any major or minor amputations, any acute thromboembolism, and International Society on Thrombosis and Haemostasis major bleeding at 36 months after study enrollment. OACART trial will provide the optimal antithrombotic treatment strategy for patients with stable high-risk atherosclerosis. Clinical Research Information Service (CRIS) of Republic of Korea, KCT0008458, registered on May 22, 2023. https://cris.nih.go.kr/cris/search/detailSearch.do?seq=28968&search_page=L.

title: Measures of recovery used in clinical settings among people with opioid use disorder: a rapid review of the literature.
abstract: The United States (US) has observed increasing rates of opioid use and overdose deaths since the 1990s. For patients receiving medications for opioid use disorder (OUD), clinical visits are a critical touchpoint to evaluate progress towards recovery. This rapid review aims to identify psychometrically validated measures of recovery used in clinical settings in the US for individuals with OUD. A systematic search of Embase and Health and Psychosocial Instruments databases was conducted. peer-reviewed studies in English from 2000 to 2023 that applied recovery measures within U.S. clinical treatment settings for individuals with OUD. References were screening and data extracted using Rayyan. Identified measures were mapped to patient-centered treatment goals. 19 studies met the inclusion criteria, including 37 validated measures of recovery. Measures were predominantly designed to be self-administrated. Measures fell under three domains: exclusively measuring drug use, measuring drug use and other factors, and exclusively measuring factors other than drug use. The most used measure was the Addiction Severity Index, used in 10 studies. After mapping to established patient-centered treatment goals, avoid illicit drug use (n = 14, 38%) was the construct identified most frequently across included measures. This rapid review of OUD recovery measures found a wide range of measures used over the study period. The most used measures focused on frequency and severity of drug use. Patient-centered treatment goals were largely covered by identified measures. Self-administer design of most measures presents opportunity to leverage patient-reported outcomes in clinical settings to evaluate recovery and inform treatment plans. Future research should explore how customizable PROMs and PREMs for patients in treatment for OUD can support goal tracking, improve patient-clinician decision-making, and help patients with recovery. Not applicable.

title: ME/CFS and the thalamus as a precision gate: what reversible thalamocortical connectivity reveals about central gain in post-infectious fatigue.
abstract: Kim and colleagues report a finding that is easy to understate: thalamic hyperconnectivity with sensorimotor and visuo-occipital cortices, present in patients with myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome (ME/CFS) at baseline, shifts back toward the pattern seen in healthy controls after hyperbaric oxygen therapy and does so most in the patients who improve clinically. To my knowledge, this is the first treatment-coupled, apparently reversible thalamocortical signature in ME/CFS. Viewed through predictive processing (the framework in which the brain continually predicts its own sensory and bodily inputs), the thalamus is theorised to be a gain-control gate that helps set the precision or weight assigned to ascending bodily signals. I argue that the baseline hyperconnectivity reflects deficient filtering of expected input, and that its post-treatment reduction may index restored filtering. The same failure of attenuation offers a parsimonious account of several symptoms that often co-occur in patients, including sensory hypersensitivity, pain, orthostatic intolerance, and cognitive "brain fog", as one mechanism expressed across exteroceptive, nociceptive, autonomic, and cognitive domains. Because hyperbaric oxygen therapy is a vascular intervention and resting-state connectivity is an indirect measure this gain interpretation remains a hypothesis and I outline how it can be tested across exertion and post-exertional malaise rather than at baseline alone.

title: Genome-wide association study of human papillomavirus infection and persistence in women living with HIV in Rwanda.
abstract: We conducted an explorative genome-wide association study (GWAS) in East Africa to identify host genetic variants associated with the acquisition and persistence of human papillomavirus (HPV) infection. We genotyped 385 Rwandan women living with HIV and selected host biomarker assay signals from genital swab samples using qPCR. We compared women who cleared HPV over a two-year interval (operationally defined as persistent infection), with those who did not. Exploratory gene-based aggregation analyses of rare and low-frequency variants represented on the genotyping array were also performed. In the primary cluster-stratified Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel analysis, rs13158830 within PPARGC1B exceeded the conventional genome-wide significance threshold for persistent HPV infection. The nearby MIR378A gene-expression assay signal was higher in HPV-positive women but did not distinguish clearance from persistence. We identified an exploratory host genetic association with persistent HPV infection and several additional candidate loci. The lead rs13158830 signal remained evident in Fisher exact testing and PC-adjusted Firth regression, but the small number of carriers produced substantial uncertainty. These findings require replication in independent cohorts. Not applicable.

title: Effectiveness of using bite turbos on temporary implant crowns for intrusion in clear aligner therapy: a clinical retrospective study.
abstract: This retrospective study aimed to evaluate whether aligner-incorporated bite turbos placed on implant-supported temporary crowns improve the predictability of maxillary molar intrusion during clear aligner treatment (CAT). 80 adult patients treated with clear aligners were included and divided into two groups: no-BT (n = 45) and bite turbo (BT) (n = 35). Digital models were superimposed using palatal rugae-based registration in OnyxCeph (Image Instruments, Chemnitz, Germany). Planned and achieved intrusion, lack of correction, and molar inclination were analyzed. Intra- and inter-examiner reliability were assessed using the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC). No statistically significant differences were observed between BT and control groups in planned intrusion (p = 0.184), lack of correction (p = 0.953), or achieved inclination (p = 0.137). Within the limitations of this retrospective study, aligner-incorporated bite turbos on temporary prosthetic crowns did not significantly improve elongated maxillary molar intrusion during clear aligner therapy.

title: Blocking the microglia-endothelial axis via SPP1-ITGAV disruption attenuates neuroinflammation in multiple sclerosis.
abstract: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a chronic demyelinating disorder of the central nervous system (CNS) characterized by persistent neuroinflammation and immune cell infiltration. Despite extensive study, the specific mechanisms by which local microenvironmental signals enable peripheral immune cells to breach the blood-brain barrier (BBB)-especially without overt structural disruption-are not fully understood. We utilized integrated transcriptomic analysis to identify specific microglia populations in demyelinating lesions. In vitro cellular models, coupled with confocal microscopy and biochemical analyses, were employed to investigate the interaction between microglia-derived factors and vascular endothelial cells, specifically evaluating adhesion molecule dynamics and transendothelial migration. In vivo validation was performed using an experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (EAE) mouse model to assess the effects of targeted pharmacological inhibition on immune cell infiltration and clinical disease severity. We identified a distinct MS-inflamed microglia (MIMS) population characterized by high expression of secreted phosphoprotein 1 (SPP1, osteopontin), which is markedly increased in chronic lesions. Integrated transcriptomic and in vitro experiments revealed that microglial SPP1 acts on endothelial cells via an interaction with the Integrin αVβ1 (ITGAV/ITGB1) receptor complex. Mechanistically, this engagement activates the Focal Adhesion Kinase (FAK)/NF-κB signaling cascade, driving the robust expression and dynamic turnover of endothelial adhesion molecules. Crucially, this SPP1-driven endothelial activation enables the massive, pan-lineage recruitment of circulating immune cells without evidence of overt barrier disruption. Furthermore, in vivo intrathecal inhibition of SPP1 significantly reduced peripheral immune cell migration into the CNS and alleviated disease severity in the EAE model. CNS-resident microglia actively instruct the vascular endothelium via the SPP1-ITGAV-FAK axis to orchestrate peripheral immune cell entry without overt barrier disruption. These findings provide insights into neuro-immune crosstalk at the BBB and highlight a potential targetable pathway for modifying compartmentalized neuroinflammatory diseases.

title: The impact of negative life events on adolescents and young adults affective disorders: a moderated mediation analysis.
abstract: Adolescent negative life events are important risk factors for affective disorders. However, it remains unclear whether visual comprehension mediates the relationship between negative life events and affective disorders. This study proposed that visual comprehension mediates the relationship between negative life events and affective disorders and that higher-level comprehensive control moderates this model. It also compared the dominant positions of the visual and auditory response control. Data were collected from 101 adolescent and young adult participants with first-episode depressive disorders attending a health centre outpatient department; of these, 84 met the inclusion criteria and were included in the final sample. Negative life event levels was assessed using the Adolescent Self-Rating Life Events Checklist (ASLEC) and affective disorders, Self-Rating Depression Scale, Self-Rating Anxiety Scale, and Symptom Checklist-90. Cognitive function was quantified using an integrated continuous visual and auditory performance test. The moderated mediation model comprised ASLEC as the independent variable; affective disorder, dependent; visual comprehension quotient (VCQ), mediator; and full-scale response control quotient (FSRCQ) and auditory response control quotients (ARCQ), moderators. VCQ mediated the relationship between ASLEC and affective disorders. FSRCQ moderated the overall model and the association between ASLEC and VCQ. ARCQ also moderated this model. Negative life events significantly positively correlated with affective disorders, with higher levels predicting higher severity. Moreover, visual comprehension facilitated this relationship, with an increase in negative life events significantly weakening visual comprehension, thereby exacerbating affective disorders. Individuals with higher comprehensive and auditory response controls showed stronger inhibitory effect of negative life events on visual comprehension. This study provides preliminary empirical evidence of the relationship between negative life events, cognitive function, and affective disorders. Cognitive function mediates negative life events' impact on affective disorders in adolescents and young adults. In particular, auditory response control moderates the association between negative life events and visual comprehension.

title: Environmental and genetic interactions in autism spectrum disorder: a literature review with a focus on air pollution.
journal: Environmental health : a global access science source
abstract: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is a neurodevelopmental condition which is associated with complex interactions between genetic susceptibility and environmental exposures. More recently, air pollution has been investigated as a modifiable risk factor and contributor to the neurodevelopmental outcomes of the disorder. This review focuses on the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region and discusses genetic, immunologic, and epigenetic findings that help explain how pollutants, including particulate matter (PM₂.₅, PM₁₀), nitrogen oxides, ozone, and dioxins, contribute to the pathogenesis of ASD and its specific involvement in neuronal pathways. Many pollutants have been found to increase oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, and endocrine disruption which alters DNA methylation and histone modification patterns. The pathology of this involves activation of the aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR) and its downstream CYP1A1/CYP1B1 pathways which link environmental to altered gene expression and neural circuits. Current studies have shown that prenatal and early postnatal exposures are critical windows in which air pollutants can impair synaptogenesis, microglial regulation, and neurotransmitter balance. Significantly, sex-specific differences further modulate susceptibility, with males demonstrating heightened vulnerability due to hormonal and immune interactions. While progress has been made in uncovering these mechanisms, challenge in establishing causality and addressing diagnostic biases persists. Future directions should integrate longitudinal cohorts, omics-based biomarkers, and machine-learning models to clarify exposure-response relationships and guide personalized prevention strategies. Understanding how environmental and genetic factors converge to disrupt neurodevelopment is essential to mitigating ASD risk in increasingly polluted environments.

title: Advances in modified anti-Aβ antibodies for the treatment of Alzheimer's disease.
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a progressive and irreversible neurodegenerative disorder, the treatment of which remains a major clinical challenge. In recent years, significant progress has been made in the immunotherapy of AD. Notably, monoclonal antibodies targeting amyloid-β (Aβ) have already been applied in clinical practice. However, as macromolecular therapeutics, antibodies face substantial challenges in crossing the blood-brain barrier (BBB) efficiently. Systemic administration typically requires high dosages to achieve the therapeutic level of brain exposure, which may trigger adverse events such as amyloid-related imaging abnormalities (ARIA) and thus restrict their widespread clinical application. To resolve this problem, various engineering strategies for modifying anti-Aβ antibodies have been developed. This review summarizes four major modification categories: BBB-penetrating bispecific antibodies (BsAbs), glycosylation engineering, antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs), and chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-based cell therapies (including CAR-macrophages, CAR-T cells, and CAR-astrocytes). We provide an in-depth discussion of their delivery efficiency, targeting capability, and safety, aiming to lay a foundation for developing safer and more effective next-generation anti-Aβ antibody therapeutic strategies.

title: Preoperative factors associated with quadriceps strength 1 year after total knee arthroplasty: a prospective longitudinal study.
abstract: Quadriceps strength is highly related to physical function following total knee arthroplasty (TKA). Preoperative factors associated with long-term postoperative strength remain insufficiently understood. The aim of this exploratory study was to investigate preoperative factors associated with normalized quadriceps strength (NQS), changes in NQS and limb symmetry index (LSI) 1 year after TKA in patients with uncomplicated recovery. A prospective longitudinal study was conducted. Measurements took place at three primary care rehabilitation facilities in Region Västra Götaland, Sweden. The final analysis included 39 participants aged 65 years or older who underwent elective fast-track primary TKA due to knee osteoarthritis and had an uncomplicated recovery. Preoperative factors associated with NQS in the operated limb after 1 year (n = 39), changes in NQS from preoperative testing to 1 year after TKA (n = 39), and LSI (n = 35) were analyzed in three separate exploratory multiple linear regression models. Preoperative factors included age, sex, NQS, the 6-minute walk test (6MWT), and the LSI. Preoperative NQS (B = 0.72, 95% CI: 0.40 to 1.0, p < 0.001) and LSI (B = - 0.17, 95% CI: - 0.29 to - 0.037, p = 0.013) were significantly associated with NQS 1 year after TKA. LSI was the only preoperative factor significantly associated with changes in NQS (B = - 0.19, 95% CI: - 0.32 to - 0.059, p = 0.006) and LSI 1 year after TKA (B = 0.41, 95% CI: 0.15 to 0.68, p = 0.004). In this selected and relatively small sample, greater normalized quadriceps strength in the operated limb and higher LSI 1 year after TKA appeared to be primarily associated with higher preoperative normalized quadriceps strength in the operated limb and higher preoperative LSI, respectively, whereas strength gains appeared to be associated with lower preoperative LSI. The findings should be considered exploratory and primarily applicable to older adults with uncomplicated recovery after TKA. Confirmation in larger studies is warranted. Retrospectively registered February 9, 2022 ( http://clinicaltrials.gov , ID: NCT05248815).

title: Young adults with OCD and their experiences of the school-to-work or university transition: an explorative qualitative study.
abstract: The school-to-work or school-to-university transition (STWT) can be a challenging process for young adults, especially for those suffering from mental disorders such as obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD). While OCD is a relatively common disorder, little is known about how young adults with OCD experience the STWT process. A better understanding of the conditions influencing STWT may deepen knowledge relevant to the development and implementation of interventions aiming at promoting labour market inclusion for this population. This study aimed to explore how young adults aged 19-29 years living with OCD experience the STWT and which factors they perceive as challenging or supportive during this process. The study employed an explorative qualitative design. Data were collected through semi-structured individual interviews with 21 participants (14 females and 7 males) diagnosed with OCD, with a mean age of 23.0 years at the time of the interviews. Data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis. Two themes were generated: (1) Navigating pathways into the labour market through studies or work while managing health and (2) Navigating pathways into the labour market through societal support. The analysis illustrates how OCD symptoms, as well as organisational and societal conditions, could create challenges that affected and, in some cases, delayed the STWT process. Participants struggled to manage these challenges while also prioritising their health. Throughout this process, they developed their own strategies and used various forms of support. The findings suggest a potential interplay between OCD symptoms and engagement in education and employment during the STWT process. Increased OCD symptoms, worsening mental health, and unmet individual needs may contribute to delay or interrupt the transition. Individual coping strategies, pedagogical, workplace-related, social and societal support may help young adults overcome challenges while maintaining their mental health and well-being. The findings emphasise the need for flexible, individualised support and coordinated efforts among relevant stakeholders. Healthcare services may address both symptom management and the new contexts and challenges embedded in the transition. Increased awareness of OCD, together with sustainable and supportive study and work environments, is important for improving inclusion in working life among young adults with OCD.

title: Spectrum of amyloid-related imaging abnormalities associated with aducanumab treatment: a case series report.
abstract: Amyloid-related imaging abnormalities (ARIA) observed on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) are known adverse events associated with beta-amyloid plaque-lowering monoclonal antibodies. A spectrum of radiographic and clinical presentations of ARIA have been observed. ARIA-E refer to vasogenic edema in the brain parenchyma and/or leptomeningeal/subpial sulcal effusion; ARIA-H refer to hemosiderin deposits including cerebral microhemorrhage and localized superficial siderosis. With clinical availability of anti-amyloid therapies for treatment of early clinical stage Alzheimer's disease, there is an important need for better awareness of ARIA and education among a diversity of clinicians and practice settings. To illustrate the wide spectrum of ARIA, we present the clinical history, course, and MRI findings as well as summarize learnings and implications of 10 ARIA-E cases from the aducanumab phase 3 clinical trials EMERGE and ENGAGE (ClinicalTrials.gov identifiers NCT02484547 and NCT02477800). Monitoring and management of ARIA, including criteria and timing of MRI, and drug dosing actions were defined per protocol and based upon radiographic severity and clinical symptoms associated with ARIA. ARIA were detected by MRI performed at pre-specified intervals or in response to symptoms or for safety follow-up reasons. The majority of ARIA-E events were asymptomatic. Most ARIA-E events occurred within the first 8 aducanumab doses and generally resolved within 3-4 months whether dosing was continued (i.e. when ARIA-E was asymptomatic and of mild radiographic severity) or whether dosing was suspended or discontinued. Occasionally, ARIA-E were recurrent. ARIA-H (microhemorrhages and superficial siderosis) most commonly occurred concurrently with ARIA-E. However, ARIA-H without ARIA-E, termed isolated ARIA-H, occurred at a similar frequency in aducanumab- and placebo-treated groups. 10% of participants with ARIA in the 10 mg/kg group had accompanying symptoms. When present, symptoms of ARIA most frequently included headache, nausea, fatigue, dizziness, confusional state, and visual disturbance. Serious symptoms associated with ARIA were uncommon (occurring in 0.3% of the participants treated with the 10 mg/kg dose regimen). These illustrative cases provide learnings into the nature and factors associated with ARIA that can increase knowledge for clinicians and trialists regarding the varied radiographic and clinical presentations and evolution of ARIA. Clinical Trials NCT02484547, registered June 18, 2015, https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02484547 . Clinical Trials NCT02477800, registered June 18, 2015, https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02477800 .

title: Prenatal antiseizure medication exposure and offspring structural and neurodevelopmental outcomes: an umbrella review of systematic reviews and meta-analyses.
abstract: Review-level evidence on prenatal antiseizure medication (ASM) exposure is difficult to interpret because outcome domains are often synthesized separately, primary studies overlap, and comparator frameworks and certainty vary. We aimed to calibrate evidence across structural and neurodevelopmental outcomes. We conducted an anchor-based umbrella review of systematic reviews and meta-analyses (PROSPERO: CRD420251142541), searching four databases through December 31, 2025. One prespecified anchor review represented each drug-outcome-comparator question; overlapping reviews were not combined into second-order pooled estimates. AMSTAR 2, corrected covered area, GRADE, and directional umbrella-credibility classes were applied, with NS assigned when the 95% confidence interval included the null. Fourteen reviews were included: nine structural and five neurodevelopmental. All had Low or Critically Low AMSTAR 2 confidence, and ASD/ADHD review overlap was very high (CCA, 28.1%). Valproate showed the most consistent retained pattern, including Class I credibility for combined major congenital anomalies and the most credible retained neurodevelopmental signal for autism spectrum disorder (adjusted hazard ratio, 3.10; 95% CI, 2.24-4.28; Low certainty; Class II). Topiramate showed an oral-cleft signal with Low certainty and Class III credibility. The lamotrigine estimate for major congenital anomalies was NS, whereas the orofacial-cleft estimate excluded the null but had Very Low certainty (OR, 1.42; 95% CI, 1.05-1.92; Class IV). Other retained neurodevelopmental anchors had Very Low certainty and were Class IV or NS; no independent pairwise neurodevelopmental anchor was available for carbamazepine, oxcarbazepine, topiramate, or levetiracetam. Review-level evidence was most consistent for valproate and aligned with its established structural and neurodevelopmental risks. NS or Very Low-certainty findings for non-valproate ASMs should not be interpreted as evidence of no risk. Comparative safety requires individualized risk-benefit assessment rather than binary safety classifications.

title: Growing Proficiency in Tic Disorder Care and Skills (GP-TiCS): a thematic analysis of patient and professional group experiences in primary care for primary tic disorders.
abstract: Around 300,000 people in the UK are thought to be living with Tourette syndrome (TS). Many people with tics and their families report negative experiences when approaching their general practitioner (GP) for advice and support. Limited education during medical training coupled with a lack of National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) guidelines for tic disorders (TD) creates clinical challenges for healthcare professionals (HCPs). Building on the results of an international systematic review of healthcare experiences for tics, this study aimed to further explore patient and professional experiences in primary care in England, specifically. A thematic analysis was conducted on interviews with adults with tics (n = 5), parents of children and young people (CYP) with tics (n = 5), GPs (n = 6), and secondary care HCPs working with people with tics (n = 4). The Factors Impacting GPs' Knowledge and Education of Tics theme suggested that limited education and guidance made it more difficult for GPs to support people presenting with tics yet also considers how surmounting pressures and expectations on primary care may exceed the responsibility and capabilities of GPs. Inconsistent Availability of Support for Tics Across the Country continues to be an issue for GPs making referrals to services and for people seeking support, while secondary HCPs report receiving unclear referrals with limited information which makes service allocation more difficult. The Experiences of Primary Care for Tics theme explores how the wider impact of living with tics is often left unexplored, while stigma, communication, and signposting were all identified areas for improvement. The results suggest accessible and appropriate education opportunities for GPs may improve experience for people presenting with tics by increasing GP knowledge and awareness of tics. This study precedes the development of an online learning resource for GPs.

title: Disease-modifying interventions in psychiatry.
journal: The Australian and New Zealand journal of psychiatry
abstract: Disease-modifying interventions do not just treat the symptoms of the disease but target the underlying disease process and natural course. The construct of disease-modifying treatments has transformed the care of disorders, like rheumatoid arthritis and multiple sclerosis, by shifting the focus to preventing end-organ damage rather than offering symptomatic treatment. As mental illness may have a chronic and progressive course, there is a need to consider whether any of our interventions may be disease-modifying. We, therefore, conducted a search using databases, including MEDLINE, EMBASE and PsycINFO, to identify peer-reviewed papers and grey literature related to the research question: 'Which psychiatric treatments are disease-modifying?' Disease-modifying properties were largely operationalised around end-organ changes, including structural brain changes evident on neuroimaging and cognition, and were reported for conventional psychotropics, as well as for novel pharmaceuticals and non-pharmacological interventions. Lithium and electroconvulsive therapy showed the greatest evidence as disease-modifying interventions. However, to establish this and identify potential other disease-modifying treatments, there needs to be a shift in the focus of psychiatric clinical trials to include primary outcomes that reflect disease progression and not just acute symptom burden. The potential disease-modifying properties of lithium and electroconvulsive therapy should spur the prioritisation of treatment higher up the algorithm, as well as the commencement of disease-modifying therapy as early as possible in the illness course to prevent adverse outcomes.

title: Aerobic exercise training alters gastrointestinal microbiota and enhances exercise capacity in UM-HET3 mice.
abstract: Aerobic exercise attenuates age-related physiological decline, potentially through favorable modulation of gut microbiota diversity. The purpose of this study was to characterize aerobic exercise training (ET)-induced alterations in the gut microbiome of aging, genetically heterogeneous UM-HET3 mice and examine associations between microbial shifts and changes in body composition (body weight, lean mass, and fat mass) and exercise capacity (total work, distance, and duration). Male UM-HET3 mice were assigned to sedentary (SED; n = 16) or ET (n = 17) groups. ET mice trained 5 days per week for 4 weeks at 65% of maximal work output. Body composition and exercise capacity were assessed before and after the intervention. Post-intervention fecal samples were analyzed by 16S rRNA gene sequencing (SED, n = 13; ET, n = 13). ASVs were taxonomically classified using QIIME2 with the SILVA 138.1 reference database. Alpha and beta diversity analyses were conducted in R, and Spearman's correlations assessed relationships between phylum-level abundances and physiological outcomes. ET mice exhibited greater alpha diversity, with a higher median richness (219.5), although differences were not statistically significant. Principal coordinate analysis of beta diversity demonstrated significant separation between groups (P = 0.01), indicating distinct microbial community composition. At the phylum level, ET was associated with modest shifts in gut microbial composition, characterized by higher relative abundances of Firmicutes and Verrucomicrobiota and lower abundances of Bacteroidota and Desulfobacterota compared to SED mice. Collectively, these findings indicate that aerobic exercise training induces distinct shifts in gut microbiota composition in middle-aged UM-HET3 mice despite underlying genetic heterogeneity.
